confirmed.title: FilterEffect.priority is 0 (Pixi: 1), so a mask and filters on the same container can end up in the wrong order
confirmed.description: MaskEffect and FilterEffect both use priority 0 in engine2d. addEffect sorts by priority (Container.ts:1282), and Array.sort is stable, so the effect order becomes insertion order. Pixi gives every mask effect priority 0 (StencilMask, AlphaMask, ColorMask, ScissorMask) and FilterEffect priority 1, so the mask always sorts before (outside) the filters. Collector.collectWithEffects (src/engine2d/gpu/collect.ts:168-180) pushes and pops effects in array order. On the branch, a container that gets filters before a mask, or has its mask cleared and set again while filtered, renders with the filter outside the mask. Pixi always renders with the mask outside the filter.
confirmed.reference: node_modules/pixi.js/lib/filters/FilterEffect.mjs:7 (this.priority = 1); node_modules/pixi.js/lib/rendering/mask/stencil/StencilMask.mjs:9 and alpha/AlphaMask.mjs:9 (priority = 0); node_modules/pixi.js/lib/scene/container/container-mixins/effectsMixin.mjs addEffect sorts by priority
confirmed.failure_scenario: c.filters = [blur]; c.mask = g. Pixi: c.effects = [mask, filter]. engine2d: c.effects = [filters, mask], confirmed by repro tmp/review/scene-transform/prio.test.ts. Pixi clips the blurred output to the mask. engine2d blurs content that is already masked, so the blur spills past the mask edge, and the filter bounds and texture size differ. The same happens after UIScrollView-style `mask = null; ...; mask = m` on a filtered container.
confirmed.game_impact: The game does not hit this today. The masked nodes are ObjectExamineScene.viewLayer, DevModeUI.contentContainer, DialogueUI.bodyText, the InventoryUI nameText mask, and UIScrollView.content. None of them ever gets .filters: the game's .filters assignments go to sprites, NPC and player containers, objectRoot, bgSprite, castMesh and similar, and none of those nodes is masked. It is a latent divergence with a one-line fix.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Set `priority = 1` on FilterEffect, matching Pixi.

primary.reasoning:
The finding holds. The branch sets `FilterEffect.priority = 0` at src/engine2d/scene/Container.ts:133, the same value as MaskEffect at :96. addEffect (Container.ts:1279-1284) does a stable sort by priority, so the effects keep the order they were added in. Pixi sets `this.priority = 1` on FilterEffect (node_modules/pixi.js/lib/filters/FilterEffect.mjs:7) and uses the same stable sort (effectsMixin.mjs:22), so the mask always comes first. Collector.collectWithEffects (src/engine2d/gpu/collect.ts:167-182) pushes effects in array order and pops them in reverse, so array index 0 is the outermost effect.

The repro creates Pixi and engine2d containers side by side and prints their effects:
- `filters = [f]; mask = g` gives Pixi `['stencilMask','filter']` with priorities [0,1], and engine2d `['filters','mask']` with priorities [0,0].
- `mask = g; filters = [f]; mask = null; mask = g2` gives Pixi `['stencilMask','filter']` and engine2d `['filters','mask']`.

So on the branch the filter wraps the mask instead of the mask wrapping the filter. That changes the filter bounds and lets filter output (for example a blur) spread past the mask edge.

The game does not hit this path. The containers that get masks are UIScrollView.content (UIScrollView.ts:93, 158-160), InventoryUI nameText (InventoryUI.ts:465), DevModeUI.contentContainer (DevModeUI.ts:290 and others), DialogueUI.bodyText (DialogueUI.ts:811) and ObjectExamineScene.viewLayer (ObjectExamineScene.ts:401). None of them is ever given `.filters`.

The containers that get filters are all different nodes:
- `worldContainer`, through WorldFilterPipeline (Renderer.ts:79)
- `renderer.backgroundLayer` (DepthDebugVisualizer.ts:166)
- `objectRoot` and `bgSprite` in ObjectExamineScene; these are children of viewLayer, not viewLayer itself
- NPC and player containers (Game.ts:8090, 8189)
- SpriteEntity.sprite, EntityShadow.castMesh, Hotspot.displaySprite, and the sprites in the water minigame and irradianceProbe

No node has both a mask and filters, so the effect order never matters today. The divergence is latent and low severity, as claimed.
primary.fix_suggestion: In src/engine2d/scene/Container.ts:133 change `priority = 0;` to `priority = 1;` in class FilterEffect, matching Pixi 8.17 FilterEffect.mjs:7. MaskEffect stays at 0, so addEffect's sort always places the mask outside the filters.

confirmed.title: destroy() resets the mask's includeInBuild and measurable; Pixi leaves the mask hidden
confirmed.description: When a masked container is destroyed, engine2d calls this._maskEffect.reset(), which sets mask.measurable = true and mask.includeInBuild = true. Pixi's Container.destroy only sets `this._maskEffect = null` and never resets or returns the effect. In Pixi the mask object stays includeInBuild = false (not drawn, not measured) after the masked container is destroyed.
confirmed.reference: node_modules/pixi.js/lib/scene/container/Container.mjs destroy(): `this._maskEffect = null; this._filterEffect = null; this.effects = null;` with no reset(). StencilMask.reset() (rendering/mask/stencil/StencilMask.mjs) is only called through the mask setter's MaskEffectManager.returnMaskEffect.
confirmed.failure_scenario: parent.addChild(maskG, content); content.mask = maskG; content.destroy(). Pixi: maskG stays in parent and stays invisible. engine2d: maskG is drawn again as a solid white shape, and it now counts toward parent.getBounds() and getLocalBounds().
confirmed.game_impact: The game does not hit this today. DevModeUI.clearChildren destroys contentMask first. DialogueUI, InventoryUI and UIScrollView destroy the mask and the masked node together through destroy({children:true}) or a whole-panel rebuild, which removes the mask from the tree before the reset runs. ObjectExamineScene clears viewLayer.mask explicitly. The branch's behaviour is arguably saner, but it differs from Pixi.

primary.reasoning:
Confirmed, with a side-by-side repro. The divergence is real, but the game never observes it.

Code evidence:
- src/engine2d/scene/Container.ts:1383-1386: destroy() calls `this._maskEffect.reset()`. MaskEffect.reset() at Container.ts:104-107 sets `mask.measurable = true` and `mask.includeInBuild = true`.
- Pixi's destroy() (node_modules/pixi.js/lib/scene/container/Container.mjs:1142) only runs `this._maskEffect = null`. StencilMask.reset(), which restores the two flags, runs only through the mask setter and returnMaskEffect.

Repro: .claude/review-repros/engine2d-r1/verify-scene-transform-1/maskDestroy.test.ts
- Setup: parent.addChild(maskG 500x500, content 10x10); content.mask = maskG; content.destroy().
- engine2d afterwards: `{inc:true, meas:true, parent localBounds w:500, inParent:true}`. The mask is drawn and measured again.
- Pixi 8.17 afterwards: `{inc:false, meas:false, w:0, inParent:true}`. The mask stays hidden and unmeasured.
- Both libraries match before the destroy (`inc:false, meas:false, w:10`).

Game impact: none observable. Every mask site either clears the mask first or destroys the mask with the masked node or before it:
- UIScrollView.ts:441 sets `content.mask = null` before `container.destroy({children:true})`.
- DevModeUI.clearChildren (DevModeUI.ts:166-168) destroys contentMask before anything else.
- ObjectExamineScene.ts:758 sets `viewLayer.mask = null`.
- DialogueUI.ts:1334 runs `container.destroy({children:true})`. Parent destroy calls removeChildren before destroying each child, so bodyMask (a sibling in textLayer) is already detached when bodyText's destroy resets it, and bodyMask is destroyed right after.
- InventoryUI.ts:465 masks nameText with a sibling nameMask in grid.content. That tree is torn down only via grid.destroy() (InventoryUI.ts:915, which goes through UIScrollView.destroy with children:true). The mask is detached and then destroyed, so the reset has no visible or bounds effect.

The reset code does run in the game (DialogueUI and InventoryUI), but it only touches masks that are already detached and about to be destroyed. No game path produces the Pixi-divergent output, so severity is low.
primary.fix_suggestion: In src/engine2d/scene/Container.ts destroy() (line 1383), replace the `if (this._maskEffect) { this._maskEffect.reset(); this._maskEffect = null; }` block with just `this._maskEffect = null;`, which matches Pixi Container.mjs:1142. Keep effect.reset() in the mask setter (Container.ts:1243), which mirrors Pixi's returnMaskEffect → StencilMask.reset(). Add a regression test: after content.destroy(), maskG.includeInBuild and maskG.measurable stay false and parent.getLocalBounds() excludes maskG.

confirmed.title: Filter-area bounds (fastBoundsRecursive) include setActive(false) subtrees, placed where they were last drawn
confirmed.description: The recursion that sizes a filter's area (calculateFilterArea -> fastBoundsRecursive) skips a node only when `localDisplayStatus !== 7 || !measurable`. It never checks `_activeSelf`. Every other traversal on the branch does prune inactive nodes (collect.ts:29/52, Culler.ts:49, EventBoundary.ts:430, Container.ts:1460/1492). The inactive node's `groupTransform` also goes stale, because collect.ts:52-57 returns early for inactive nodes without recomputing their transform or their children's. The result: an NPC or hotspot hidden with setActive(false) still adds its bounds to any filtered ancestor, at the place it was last drawn. On master the same entity is hidden with visible=false, which clears bit1 of localDisplayStatus, so Pixi's `_getGlobalBoundsRecursive` leaves it out.
confirmed.reference: node_modules/pixi.js/lib/scene/container/container-mixins/getFastGlobalBoundsMixin.mjs:22 (`if (this.localDisplayStatus !== 7 || !this.measurable) return;` — master hides NPCs/hotspots via visible=false, so they are excluded); master src/entities/Npc.ts:652 and src/entities/Hotspot.ts:420 wrote container.visible.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Repro at tmp/review/hierarchy-entities/filterBounds.test.ts (NullRhiDevice). Setup: layer holds a 4x4 sprite at the origin and an 'npc' container with a 4x4 sprite at (40,40). Render once, hide the npc, set layer.filters=[AlphaFilter], render again. If the npc is hidden with visible=false (the Pixi/master equivalent), the filter texture is 4x4. If it is hidden with setActive(false), the texture is 64x64 because the bounds cover (0,0)-(44,44). The test fails with `expected ['64x64'] to deeply equal ['4x4']`.
confirmed.game_impact: The game does reach this path. SceneManager.ts:1954 calls renderer.loadAndSetWorldFilter(filterId), which puts a ColorMatrixFilter on worldContainer, the ancestor of entityLayer and so of every NPC/hotspot container. Scenes that do this: 雾津街头, 码头白天, teahouse, dev_teahouse_alive, test_room_a (filters day / teahouse_evening / identity). Hidden NPCs and hotspots (schedule, conditions, pickup) therefore enlarge the world filter's area. I expect no visible difference: the area is clipped to the viewport, the background normally already fills the viewport, and all three filter JSONs have an identity alpha row ([0,0,0,1,0]), so pixels that were transparent stay transparent. The only effect I expect is a larger filter texture and more fill when the background does not cover the viewport (letterboxed or small scenes). That makes it low severity today. It would become visible with any future filter on an entity ancestor that changes transparent pixels (for example a blur, or a matrix with an alpha offset), or once the filter area is no longer clipped to the viewport.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In fastBoundsRecursive, prune on `!c._activeSelf` as well, i.e. `if (!c._activeSelf || c.localDisplayStatus !== 7 || !c.measurable) return;`, so it matches the other traversals and never reads the stale groupTransform of inactive subtrees. Add the repro as a regression test.

primary.reasoning:
Code: src/engine2d/gpu/FrameBuilder.ts:950-951 `fastBoundsRecursive` prunes only on `c.localDisplayStatus !== 7 || !c.measurable`. setActive (Container.ts:481-483) toggles `_activeSelf` and leaves localDisplayStatus alone. So an inactive subtree still gets walked. Its groupTransform is also stale, because collect.ts:52-57 (updateChild) returns early for `!_activeSelf` without recomputing any transform in that subtree. The other traversals do prune on `_activeSelf`: collect.ts:29/52, Container.ts:1460/1492 (getBounds). On master, Npc.ts:652 and Hotspot.ts:420 hid the entity with `container.visible=false`, which clears bit 2 of localDisplayStatus. Pixi's _getGlobalBoundsRecursive (getFastGlobalBoundsMixin.mjs:22) then skips it.

Repro: .claude/review-repros/engine2d-r1/verify-hierarchy-entities-0/filterBounds.test.ts (NullRhiDevice, 128x128 canvas). The layer holds a 4x4 sprite at the origin and an npc container with a 4x4 sprite at (40,40). I render once, hide the npc, add an AlphaFilter (padding 0) and render again. I then check the size of the filter texture passed to rhi.createTexture:
- shown -> 64x64
- visible=false -> 4x4
- setActive(false) -> 64x64
- setActive(false) plus moving the npc to (100,100) after hiding -> still 64x64. This confirms the stale transform: bounds sit at the last-drawn (40,40), not the current position, which would need 128x128.

Pixi side by side: `layer.getFastGlobalBounds` with a render group gives [0,0,44,44] when shown and [0,0,4,4] when visible=false. So the branch with setActive diverges from the master/Pixi equivalent. The test fails with `expected ['64x64'] to deeply equal ['4x4']`.

Game path: Npc.applyEffectiveVisible (src/entities/Npc.ts:660) and Hotspot.applyEffectiveActive (src/entities/Hotspot.ts:425) now call container.setActive. The only filter placed on an ancestor with children is the world filter. SceneManager.ts:1954 calls Renderer.loadAndSetWorldFilter (Renderer.ts:432), then WorldFilterPipeline (src/rendering/filter/WorldFilterPipeline.ts:21) sets worldContainer.filters. The other filters sit on leaves (SpriteEntity.ts:1667 sprite, EntityShadow.ts:1143 castMesh, irradianceProbe.ts:38 sprite), so this bug does not touch them. Filter-area clipping: clipToViewport defaults to true (FrameBuilder.ts:883 fitBounds), so the enlarged area is clamped to the viewport. All three filter JSONs (day, identity, teahouse_evening) have an identity alpha row [0,0,0,1,0]. The extra pixels are transparent input, stay alpha 0 after the matrix and mix, and composite as nothing. Net effect: no visible pixel difference expected, only a larger intermediate texture and extra fill when the scene content does not already cover the viewport. Severity low, as claimed. It becomes visible only with a future ancestor filter that changes transparent pixels (blur, alpha offset) or with clipToViewport=false.
primary.fix_suggestion: src/engine2d/gpu/FrameBuilder.ts:951 — change the guard to `if (!c._activeSelf || c.localDisplayStatus !== 7 || !c.measurable) return;`. This matches collect.ts/getBounds pruning and never reads the stale groupTransform of inactive subtrees. With it, a setActive(false) subtree is excluded exactly as Pixi excludes a visible=false one. Add the repro (the texture size with setActive(false) should equal the visible=false result, 4x4) as a regression test next to src/engine2d/gpu/msaa.test.ts.

confirmed.title: Sprite roundPixels is read live every frame; Pixi snapshots it when the sprite is first drawn, so the player sprite never rounds on master
confirmed.description: Pixi 8.17 SpritePipe._initGPUSprite sets `batchableSprite.roundPixels = renderer._roundPixels | sprite._roundPixels` once, when the BatchableSprite is created at the sprite's first collected render. Nothing updates it afterwards: ViewContainer's roundPixels setter only stores `_roundPixels`, and _updateBatchableSprite only refreshes bounds and texture. Mesh, NineSlice and CanvasText pipes do the same. The branch copies `this._roundPixels` into the batchable on every collect (Sprite.ts:141, also Mesh.ts:145, NineSliceSprite.ts:276, Text.ts:112, HTMLText.ts:113). As a result, toggling roundPixels after a sprite's first render changes branch output but has no effect on master.
confirmed.reference: pixi.js/lib/scene/sprite/SpritePipe.mjs _initGPUSprite (roundPixels captured once), _updateBatchableSprite (bounds/texture only); scene/view/ViewContainer.mjs:55-58 (setter has no view update)
confirmed.failure_scenario: Repro in tmp/review/collect-batch/round.test.ts (passes). Pixi: first _getGpuSprite gives roundPixels 0; after `spr.roundPixels = true` the same BatchableSprite still has 0. engine2d: collects give [0, 1]. Game sequence: setupPlayer adds player.sprite.container to entityLayer (Game.ts:6202) before the first scene loads. Frames render under the loading overlay while getBackgroundTexelsPerWorld() is null, so the sprite is snapshotted with roundPixels 0. syncEntityPixelDensityMatch then runs every tick (Game.ts:10684) with entityPixelDensityMatch=true (game_config.json:19) and sets sprite.roundPixels = true (SpriteEntity.ts:1626). Master keeps drawing the player un-rounded; the branch snaps vertices to device pixels (up to 0.5px shift, and stair-step motion against the un-rounded background while walking or during camera follow).
confirmed.game_impact: Player sprite (SpriteEntity.sprite is created once, SpriteEntity.ts:346). NPC sprites and Hotspot.displaySprite (Hotspot.ts:336/344) are affected the same way whenever they are first drawn before the first sync. The difference is only visible where the sprite itself renders, i.e. scenes where the lit quad is not active (SpriteEntity.refreshLitQuad sets sprite.renderable=false when a lighting provider exists), and for hotspot display images. The F2 debug toggle (cycleEntityPixelDensityMatchDebugOverride, Game.ts:3790) is a no-op on master but live on the branch.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Latch roundPixels per view the way Pixi does: capture `renderer.roundPixels | _roundPixels` when the view is first collected and keep it until unload/destroy. Do not re-read it on each collect.

primary.reasoning:
**Repro (passes).** `npx vitest run tmp/review/verify-collect-batch-1/round.test.ts` runs the same frame sequence on both sides and reads the round bit (`textureIdAndRound & 0xffff`, vertex word 5) as it would reach the GPU.
- Pixi side: real `P.SpritePipe.addRenderable` (with `didViewUpdate` forced true), then Pixi's own `DefaultBatcher.prototype.packQuadAttributes`.
- engine2d side: a full `WebGPURenderer.render` on NullRhiDevice, reading the vertex bytes it uploads.

| Sequence | Pixi 8.17 | engine2d |
|---|---|---|
| roundPixels false, true, true | [0,0,0] | [0,1,1] |
| roundPixels true, false | [1,1] | [1,0] |

So Pixi latches the value from the first render; engine2d follows the live value.

**Code evidence.**
- Pixi `node_modules/pixi.js/lib/scene/sprite/SpritePipe.mjs:39` sets `batchableSprite.roundPixels = renderer._roundPixels | sprite._roundPixels` only in `_initGPUSprite`.
- `_updateBatchableSprite` (`SpritePipe.mjs:24-27`) refreshes only bounds and texture.
- The setter at `scene/view/ViewContainer.mjs:57-58` only stores `_roundPixels`.
- Nothing else resets it. `_gpuData` is cleared only by `unload()`/`destroy()` (`ViewContainer.mjs:92-104`). SpritePipe, unlike the NineSlice/Text/HTMLText/BitmapText pipes, is not registered with the GC through `GCManagedHash`, so a plain Sprite's latch lasts its whole life.
- Branch `src/engine2d/sprite/Sprite.ts:141` copies `this._roundPixels` into the batchable on every collect.

**Game path (master timeline, 5f5a639).**
1. `Game.start` awaits `setupPlayer`, which adds `player.sprite.container` to `entityLayer` (master `Game.ts:6221`).
2. `start` then adds `mainTick` (`Game.ts:4269`) and awaits the async scene load/boot. The Pixi Application ticker keeps rendering the stage every frame meanwhile.
3. During those frames the player sprite is collected:
   - It is visible: `Player.setVisible` has no callers.
   - It is not cullable: `Game.ts:7228` excludes the player container.
   - It is renderable: the lit quad does not exist yet.
   - `roundPixels` is still false: `syncEntityPixelDensityMatch` (`Game.ts:9269`, called every tick at `Game.ts:10772`) sets it true only once `getBackgroundTexelsPerWorld()` is non-null.
4. Result: Pixi latches 0, and the player's `Sprite` is created once and never destroyed (`SpriteEntity.ts:346`).
5. Later, `setPixelDensityMatchActive(true)` (`SpriteEntity.ts:1626`) runs with `entityPixelDensityMatch: true` (`game_config.json:19`). Master keeps drawing the player un-rounded. The branch snaps its vertices to device pixels: up to a 0.5px offset, and stair-stepped sub-pixel motion while walking or when the camera follows.
6. The F2 debug toggle (`Game.ts:3798-3800`) also changes the output on the branch but not on master.

**Visibility limit.** The difference only shows where the Sprite itself draws. When a scene has a lit payload, `refreshLitQuad` sets `sprite.renderable = false` (master `SpriteEntity.ts:576`) and a separate `LitSpriteQuad` mesh draws the player. Most scenes define `lighting` (35 of 36 scene JSONs; `dev_room.json` does not), so the visible effect is limited to scenes without a lit payload or whose bake is missing, plus dev mode.

**Unverified.** Hotspot `displaySprite` (master `Hotspot.ts:332/340`) is plausibly affected the same way, but I did not confirm whether it renders before its first sync.

**Severity.** No crash, and it is sub-pixel and limited to non-lit scenes, so medium (an edge case in a game path) stands. It is not high.

**Checked and equivalent.** Pixi GC does not touch sprite `_gpuData` (only the NineSlice/Text/HTMLText/BitmapText/Particle pipes use `GCManagedHash`). The non-batched mesh `uRound` in Pixi `MeshPipe.mjs:83` is read live, as the branch does at `FrameBuilder.ts:448/490`, so the non-batched path matches. The batched-mesh latch (`MeshPipe.mjs:115`) and the NineSlice/CanvasText/HTMLText init-time latches match the reviewer's description.
primary.fix_suggestion:
Latch the value per view the way Pixi's pipes do:

1. In engine2d `Sprite` (and likewise the batchables of `Mesh`, `NineSliceSprite`, `Text` and `HTMLText`), keep a private flag such as `_batchableInit = false`.
2. In `collectRenderables`, only when `!_batchableInit`, set `b.roundPixels = (renderer.roundPixels ? 1 : 0) | this._roundPixels` and set `_batchableInit = true`. Stop assigning `b.roundPixels` on later collects.
3. Reset `_batchableInit = false` wherever Pixi drops `_gpuData`: in `unload()` and in `destroy()`.

For exact parity on NineSlice/Text/HTMLText, which Pixi GC-manages, a reset after 60 s unused would also be needed. That is optional, since the game does not depend on it.

Add a regression test like the repro: render a sprite with `roundPixels = false`, set it to true, render again, and expect the round bit in the uploaded vertex data to stay 0.

confirmed.title: When a Sprite's non-dynamic RenderTexture is resized, the branch draws the quad at the new size but keeps the filter bounds at the old size (master keeps both at the old size)
confirmed.description: The branch recomputes the quad from `this.visualBounds` on every collect (Sprite.ts:142, updateQuadBounds with the texture's current orig/trim). Filter and hit bounds still come from the ViewContainer `bounds` cache, which is only invalidated by onViewUpdate (ViewContainer.ts:17-21; used for filter area through fastBoundsRecursive, FrameBuilder.ts:846 / Container.ts:1469). In Pixi, `batchableSprite.bounds` is the `_visualBounds` object, and it is refreshed only in _updateBatchableSprite when `didViewUpdate` is set. A non-dynamic texture (RenderTexture.create defaults to dynamic:false) that resizes emits 'update', but the Sprite only listens when texture.dynamic is true. So on master both the quad and the filter bounds stay at the old size, which is consistent but mis-scaled. On the branch the quad follows the new size while the filter bounds stay stale.
confirmed.reference: pixi.js/lib/scene/sprite/SpritePipe.mjs updateRenderable/_updateBatchableSprite (bounds refreshed only when didViewUpdate); scene/sprite/Sprite.mjs:66-80 (listens to 'update' only if dynamic) and :128-131 (visualBounds getter is the only refresh); rendering/renderers/shared/texture/RenderTexture.mjs create (dynamic ?? false)
confirmed.failure_scenario: Repro in tmp/review/collect-batch/rtResize.test.ts (passes). Start with an 800x600 RT on a Sprite and render once, then call rt.resize(600,450) and set width/height to 600/450. Pixi: quad maxX stays 800 and bounds.maxX stays 800, so the content is displayed at 800 wide. engine2d: quad maxX is 600 but bounds.maxX is still 800. When the RT grows instead (600 -> 800), the branch draws an 800-wide quad inside a filter whose input area is only 600 wide, so the right and bottom of the sprite are cropped. Master shows it complete but at the old 600 size.
confirmed.game_impact: WaterMinigameScene.layout() (WaterMinigameScene.ts:307-326) resizes bottomMrt, which bottomMrtSprite shows through waterFilter, whenever texW/texH change. layout runs on every renderer resize via subscribeAfterResize (line 199), e.g. window resize or the F2 dock squeezing #game-mount during the water minigame. On the branch the water surface gets cropped when the canvas grows; on master it is drawn at the stale size. The initial layout runs before the first render, so the start of the minigame is unaffected.
confirmed.suggested_fix: For master parity, cache visualBounds like Pixi: recompute only when onViewUpdate fired (texture/anchor change), not on every collect. Otherwise, if the fresh size is wanted, also mark _boundsDirty on texture 'update' so the quad and filter bounds agree. That would still diverge from master, so the choice should be deliberate.

primary.reasoning:
I reproduced the divergence end to end with a real engine2d WebGPURenderer on NullRhiDevice, and next to it Pixi 8.17's own SpritePipe and getFastGlobalBounds code.

Scenario (the grow case): a Sprite shows a non-dynamic RT of 600x450 and has a filter. Render once. Then call rt.resize(800,600), reassign the same texture (as layout() does, which returns early), set width/height to 900x675, and render again.
- Branch: the quad in the second collect is local 0..800 x 0..600 at scale 1.125, which is 900x675 on screen. The FrameBuilder.calculateFilterArea spy records a filter area of only 675x506.25, so the right and bottom quarter of the sprite fall outside the filter input and are cropped.
- Pixi/master: `didViewUpdate` stays false, so SpritePipe never runs `_updateBatchableSprite` again. `gpu.bounds` (the shared `_visualBounds` object) stays at 0..600, and `spr.bounds` (the filter bounds via `_getGlobalBoundsRecursive`, which reads `this.bounds`) also stays at 600x450. The quad and the filter agree, and the image is drawn at 675x506 (mis-scaled but not cropped).

Code evidence:
- Branch Sprite.ts:136-144 `collectRenderables` sets `b.bounds = this.visualBounds`, and that getter (Sprite.ts:86-89) recomputes from the current `texture.orig` on every collect.
- The branch filter bounds come from FrameBuilder.ts:945-959 `fastBoundsRecursive`, which reads `c.bounds`. That is ViewContainer.ts:16-21, cached and only dirtied by `onViewUpdate`.
- Sprite subscribes to texture 'update' only when `texture.dynamic` (Sprite.ts:70-71, same as pixi Sprite.mjs:73-74). `RenderTexture.create` defaults `dynamic` to false (branch RenderTexture.ts:6-8; pixi RenderTexture.mjs:14-19).
- In Pixi, SpritePipe.mjs:9-18 refreshes `batchableSprite.bounds` only when `didViewUpdate` is set. Only SpritePipe calls `sprite.visualBounds` inside Pixi (grep), and the game never calls `visualBounds`.

Game impact: src/systems/waterMinigame/WaterMinigameScene.ts is byte-identical to master apart from imports.
- `bottomMrt = RenderTexture.create({width:4,height:4})` (non-dynamic, line 124) is shown by `bottomMrtSprite` with `filters=[waterFilter]` (lines 132-135).
- `layout()` (288-326) resizes `bottomMrt` when `texW`/`texH` change and reassigns the same texture, which is a no-op. It then sets width/height.
- `layout()` runs on every `renderer.subscribeAfterResize` (line 199), and also at 197, 524 and 641.
- The first `layout` happens before the first render, so the minigame starts correctly. `texW`/`texH` are clamped to 256..960 and 192..720, so a resize only changes them when the viewport is smaller than roughly 1043-1084 x 753-783 CSS px (bounds are 720-800 x 480-560 in public/assets/data/water_minigames/*.json). That is common on laptop screens or with the F2 dock open.
- When the viewport grows during the minigame (window maximized, dock closed), the branch crops the right and bottom of the water surface.
- When it shrinks, the filter area is larger than the quad, where master keeps a consistent (stale) pair.

This is visible only after a resize during the minigame and depends on screen size, so severity is medium. Master is also wrong here (the image is drawn at a stale scale), but differently, so a fix toward either behaviour should be a deliberate choice.
primary.fix_suggestion: For master parity, cache the quad bounds the way Pixi's SpritePipe does. Add a dedicated flag to Sprite: `private _visualBoundsDirty = true;`. Override `onViewUpdate() { super.onViewUpdate(); this._visualBoundsDirty = true; }`. Take care that the anchor callback, the texture setter and the constructor all go through `onViewUpdate`. In `collectRenderables`, replace `b.bounds = this.visualBounds;` with `if (this._visualBoundsDirty) { updateQuadBounds(this._visualBounds, this._anchor, this._texture); this._visualBoundsDirty = false; } b.bounds = this._visualBounds;`. Keep the public `visualBounds` getter recomputing in place on the same object, as Pixi's does. Do not key the refresh off `_didViewChangeTick`: Container also increments it for child and structure changes, which in Pixi do not refresh a sprite's visual bounds. Add a regression test on NullRhiDevice: resize a non-dynamic RT after the first render and assert that the collected quad and the `calculateFilterArea` bounds both stay at the pre-resize local size. The alternative, making both fresh by also dirtying `_bounds` and the quad on the source 'resize', would fix the game visually but still differ from master, so choose it deliberately if at all.

confirmed.title: Renderer-level roundPixels is not OR'ed into batched elements
confirmed.description: Pixi batches `renderer._roundPixels | view._roundPixels` for sprites, meshes, nine-slice and text (the pipes' _init* functions). The branch passes only the view's `_roundPixels` to the Batcher. The renderer flag (WebGPURenderer.ts:199 -> FrameContext.roundPixels) is applied only to the unbatched graphics and custom mesh paths (FrameBuilder.ts:448, 490).
confirmed.reference: pixi.js/lib/scene/sprite/SpritePipe.mjs _initGPUSprite; scene/mesh/shared/MeshPipe.mjs _initBatchableMesh; scene/text/canvas/CanvasTextPipe.mjs initGpuText
confirmed.failure_scenario: Scene: new Application().init({roundPixels:true}) with a Sprite at x=10.3. Pixi snaps the quad to device pixels; engine2d draws it at the sub-pixel position.
confirmed.game_impact: None today: src/rendering/Renderer.ts:155-161 does not pass roundPixels to app.init, and no other game code sets the renderer's roundPixels.
confirmed.suggested_fix: When latching per-view roundPixels (see the snapshot finding), OR in the renderer flag.

primary.reasoning:
I reproduced this with NullRhiDevice. I built WebGPURenderer({roundPixels:true}) and rendered a Sprite(Texture.WHITE) at x=10.3, y=5.7 with sprite.roundPixels=false. I intercepted writeBuffer and read the packed textureIdAndRound vertex attribute (low 16 bits, Batcher.ts:170).
- engine2d result: {rendererOff/spriteOff: 0, rendererOn/spriteOff: 0, rendererOff/spriteOn: 1}.
- Pixi result: I ran the real pixi.js SpritePipe.prototype._initGPUSprite side by side with a stub renderer whose _roundPixels=1. It returns batchableSprite.roundPixels = 1 (SpritePipe.mjs:39: `this._renderer._roundPixels | sprite._roundPixels`).
- So with the renderer flag on and the view flag off, engine2d packs 0 where Pixi packs 1. The batch shader then skips the pixel snap (batchShader.ts:75/78).

Where the renderer flag is dropped:
- It is lost at every batched collect site: Sprite.ts:141, Mesh.ts:145, Text.ts:112, HTMLText.ts:113 and NineSliceSprite.ts:276. Each passes only this._roundPixels.
- The Pixi equivalents OR in the renderer flag: MeshPipe.mjs:115, CanvasTextPipe.mjs:64, HTMLTextPipe.mjs:87, NineSliceSpritePipe.mjs:51.
- The finding misses one more site: batched Graphics (Graphics.ts:119-122 and 132-137) also uses only this._roundPixels, while Pixi GraphicsPipe.mjs:113 uses `renderer._roundPixels | graphics._roundPixels`.
- Only the unbatched graphics path (FrameBuilder.ts:448) and the custom mesh path (FrameBuilder.ts:490) OR in ctx.roundPixels, which comes from WebGPURenderer.ts:199.

Game impact: none today.
- The only two Application.init call sites are src/rendering/Renderer.ts:155-161 and src/smell_preview_entry.ts:29-34. Neither passes roundPixels, so the renderer's _roundPixels is always 0.
- No game code sets renderer.roundPixels.
- The game only uses per-view roundPixels (SpriteEntity.ts:1626, Hotspot.ts:336/344), which the branch handles correctly (rendererOff/spriteOn gives 1 in the repro).

Severity is therefore low (an API path the game does not use).
primary.fix_suggestion:
OR the renderer flag in wherever the batched roundPixels is finally used. The smallest fix is one place: give the Batcher the frame's renderer flag (FrameContext.roundPixels, set at WebGPURenderer.ts:199). In packAttributes and packQuadAttributes (Batcher.ts:140 and 170), compute `textureIdAndRound = (textureId << 16) | ((el.roundPixels | rendererRound) & 0xffff)`.

Alternatively, OR it in at the collect sites to match Pixi's pipes: Sprite.ts:141, Mesh.ts:145, Text.ts:112, HTMLText.ts:113, NineSliceSprite.ts:276, and Graphics.ts:119/132. Those sites need access to the renderer's _roundPixels, for example through the collector. This matches SpritePipe.mjs:39, MeshPipe.mjs:115, CanvasTextPipe.mjs:64, HTMLTextPipe.mjs:87, NineSliceSpritePipe.mjs:51 and GraphicsPipe.mjs:113.

Keep the existing ctx.roundPixels OR on the unbatched and custom mesh paths (FrameBuilder.ts:448 and 490).

confirmed.title: A detached render root's own blendMode/tint is applied on the branch; Pixi ignores the root's blend and keeps a stale root vertex colour
confirmed.description: prepareTree sets `root.groupBlendMode = root.localBlendMode` (or 'normal' when inherit) and `root.groupColorAlpha = 0xffffffff`. In Pixi, the root of a detached render group is never in any childrenToUpdate list, so its groupBlendMode stays at the constructor default 'normal', and its groupColorAlpha keeps its last value (default white, or the value computed while it was in another tree). Its tint/alpha reach the draw only through renderGroup.worldColorAlpha.
confirmed.reference: pixi.js/lib/scene/container/Container.mjs:240 (groupBlendMode='normal' default); updateRenderGroupTransforms.mjs:33-53 (only worldColor/worldAlpha are computed for the root)
confirmed.failure_scenario: Repro in tmp/review/collect-batch/rootblend.test.ts (passes): a detached Sprite with blendMode='add' is enabled as a render group and updated. Pixi groupBlendMode is 'normal'; engine2d gives 'add'. Rendering such a root with renderer.render draws additively on the branch and normally on master.
confirmed.game_impact: Not hit. None of the game's offscreen roots (GiBouncePass, SceneLightingPass, shadowPrefix, backgroundSway, BurnRenderer meshes, irradianceProbe root, PlaceholderFactory container, water underwaterRtRoot) sets blendMode, tint or alpha on the root itself. In the contactAo bake, the root's vertex colour differs only in RGB, and that does not affect the AO mask alpha.

primary.reasoning:
I reproduced the divergence end to end through the renderer.

Branch code: src/engine2d/gpu/collect.ts:43-44 (prepareTree) sets `root.groupColorAlpha = 0xffffffff` and `root.groupBlendMode = root.localBlendMode === 'inherit' ? 'normal' : root.localBlendMode`.

Pixi code:
- The render-group root is never passed through updateColorBlendVisibility. updateRenderGroupTransforms.mjs:33-53 only computes renderGroup.worldColor, worldAlpha and worldColorAlpha for the root.
- So root.groupBlendMode keeps its constructor default 'normal' (Container.mjs:240), or whatever value was last computed while the root sat in another tree.
- The root's own batch reads renderable.groupBlendMode and renderable.groupColorAlpha (BatchableSprite.mjs:17,20).

Repro: .claude/review-repros/engine2d-r1/verify-collect-batch-4/rootblend.test.ts. All 4 tests pass.
- (1) In Pixi, a detached Sprite with blendMode='add', after enableRenderGroup and updateRenderGroupTransforms, has groupBlendMode 'normal', and BatchableSprite.blendMode is also 'normal'.
- (2) In Pixi, a sprite that was earlier updated under an 'add' parent keeps a stale 'add'. So Pixi's behaviour depends on history.
- (3) On the branch, `renderer.render({container: spr, target: rt})` with NullRhiDevice produces a collected batch instruction with blendMode 'add'. Master draws the same case with normal blend.
- (4) Control: a detached Container with blendMode 'add' whose child is 'inherit' is batched 'normal' on the branch. This matches Pixi's tempContainer behaviour for direct children, so the divergence is limited to the root's own drawable.

Game impact: the game does not hit this path. I checked every offscreen render root:
- GiBouncePass.ts:251, SceneLightingPass.ts:1633, shadowPrefix.ts:437/449/456, backgroundSway.ts:1112, irradianceProbe.ts:42, BurnRenderer.ts:390-391 and PlaceholderFactory.ts:68: none of these files sets blendMode, tint or alpha on the rendered root.
- WaterMinigameScene underwaterRtRoot (line 112) is a plain Container with nothing set.
- contactAo casters: the critter casters are Containers (groundLayer/bodyLayer) with no drawable of their own. The body caster is ObjectExamineScene.imageSprite, which sets tint only (ObjectExamineScene.ts:855) and no blendMode. Its root vertex colour therefore differs only in RGB from Pixi's stale groupColorAlpha, and the AO mask bake does not depend on that.
- Separately, the branch's global worldColor comes from localColor/localAlpha (WebGPURenderer.ts:204-207). For a root that has a parent, Pixi instead uses root.groupColor/groupAlpha times the parent render group's world colour. That is a related root-colour nuance, but no game root sets alpha on the rendered root, so it is not hit either.

Severity: low. It is an API edge the game never exercises.
primary.fix_suggestion: In src/engine2d/gpu/collect.ts prepareTree, stop deriving the root's blend from its own localBlendMode. When the root has no parent, set `root.groupBlendMode = 'normal'`, which is Pixi's default for a detached render-group root. When the root has a parent, the closest match to Pixi is to leave root.groupBlendMode (and groupColorAlpha) as last computed by the parent tree's pass rather than overwriting them. Keep `root.groupColorAlpha = 0xffffffff` for a parentless root, which already matches Pixi's constructor default. Children must keep using the tempContainer semantics (normal/white) as they do now. Add a regression test: a detached Sprite with blendMode 'add' rendered as root must produce a batch with blendMode 'normal'.

confirmed.title: Default (no-shader) unbatched Mesh uses identity instead of textureMatrix.mapCoord when isSimple
confirmed.description: The branch binds `tm.isSimple ? Matrix.IDENTITY : tm.mapCoord`. Pixi's GlMeshAdaptor/GpuMeshAdapter always bind `texture.textureMatrix.mapCoord`. isSimple only checks that frame == source size and rotate == 0, so a trimmed texture whose frame covers the whole source has isSimple=true but a non-identity mapCoord (the trim transform is appended).
confirmed.reference: pixi.js/lib/scene/mesh/gl/GlMeshAdaptor.mjs:41; rendering/renderers/shared/texture/TextureMatrix.mjs update() (trim appended, isSimple ignores trim)
confirmed.failure_scenario: A Mesh with no shader, more than 100 vertices, and a full-frame texture with trim: Pixi remaps the UVs into the trim rect; the branch samples the raw UVs.
confirmed.game_impact: Not hit. The only game mesh without a shader is MeshPlane in critterSim.ts:927 (7x3 = 21 vertices), which is batched, and the batched path matches Pixi (isSimple check in BatchableMesh.uvs).

primary.reasoning:
The divergence is real and I reproduced it on the NullRhiDevice.

**Code comparison.** At src/engine2d/gpu/FrameBuilder.ts:504, `drawCustom()` handles the no-shader case (`!shader`). It writes `uTextureMatrix: tm.isSimple ? Matrix.IDENTITY : tm.mapCoord`. Pixi does not have this shortcut: pixi.js/lib/scene/mesh/gl/GlMeshAdaptor.mjs:41 always sets `uTextureMatrix = texture.textureMatrix.mapCoord`. In Pixi's TextureMatrix.update(), `isSimple` (line 87) only checks that the frame is the full source size and that rotate is 0. The trim transform is still appended to `mapCoord` (lines 65-75). So a trimmed texture whose frame covers the whole source gives `isSimple=true` together with a non-identity `mapCoord`.

**Repro.** File: .claude/review-repros/engine2d-r1/verify-collect-batch-5/meshTrim.test.ts
- Texture: 16x16 BufferImageSource with frame (0,0,16,16), orig (0,0,20,20), trim (2,2,16,16).
- engine2d and Pixi agree on the texture matrix itself: both report `isSimple=true` and `mapCoord a=d=1.25, tx=ty=-0.125`.
- Mesh: engine2d Mesh with no shader on a PlaneGeometry of 11x11 = 121 vertices, so `Mesh.batched` is false (auto mode batches only up to 100 vertices, Mesh.ts:97) and it goes through `addCustom` to `drawCustom`.
- Rendered with WebGPURenderer on NullRhiDevice, with `FrameBuilder.writeUbo` spied.
- Result: the bound `uTextureMatrix` is identity (1,1,0,0). Pixi would bind (1.25,1.25,-0.125,-0.125). The test fails with exactly this difference.

**Game impact: none.**
- Every game `new Mesh(...)` passes a shader: GiBouncePass, SceneLightingPass, shadowPrefix, LitBackground, backgroundSway, Vfx*, breathingOverlayMesh, BurnRenderer, EntityShadow, CharacterLitSprite, overlayBlendShader. Those take the `resolveResources` branch, not line 504.
- The only mesh without a shader is the MeshPlane in src/systems/objectExamine/critterSim.ts:927, with `MAGGOT_VERTICES_X=7`, `MAGGOT_VERTICES_Y=3` (21 vertices). It is batched, and the batched path handles `isSimple` the same way Pixi's BatchableMesh.uvs does.
- NineSliceSprite, used in src/ui/PanelSkin.ts:188, always goes through `addBatchable` (NineSliceSprite.ts:285), never `drawCustom`.

The claimed low severity is correct.
primary.fix_suggestion: In src/engine2d/gpu/FrameBuilder.ts:504, always bind the texture matrix the way Pixi 8.17 GlMeshAdaptor/GpuMeshAdapter do: `uTextureMatrix: texture.textureMatrix.mapCoord`, and drop the `isSimple ? Matrix.IDENTITY :` shortcut. Also make sure `textureMatrix.update()` has run for the current texture before binding (Pixi's MeshPipe does this on texture update). Keep the `isSimple` check only in the batched UV path, where Pixi's BatchableMesh.uvs uses it. Add the repro above as a regression test.

confirmed.title: Filter area bounds count setActive(false) subtrees, using their stale groupTransform
confirmed.description: fastBoundsRecursive only skips a node when `c.localDisplayStatus !== 7 || !c.measurable`. It never checks `_activeSelf`. When a node is deactivated, prepareTree/updateChild (collect.ts:53-58) sets globalDisplayStatus = 0 and returns early, so it never refreshes that node's groupTransform or its children's. The filter-area pass then still walks the inactive subtree and adds each renderable's bounds at whatever groupTransform it last had: identity if it was never active, or its root-relative position (camera included) from the last frame it was active. On master, NPC and hotspot presence was `container.visible = false`, and Pixi's _getGlobalBoundsRecursive drops those nodes because localDisplayStatus is not 7. getLocalBounds and getGlobalBounds on the branch do check `_activeSelf` (Container.ts:1460, 1492); only this renderer-side copy was missed. The Npc.applyEffectiveVisible comment even states that an absent NPC should not count toward bounds.
confirmed.reference: node_modules/pixi.js/lib/scene/container/container-mixins/getFastGlobalBoundsMixin.mjs:22-24 (localDisplayStatus !== 7 -> return). Master hid NPCs and hotspots with visible=false; the branch uses setActive at src/entities/Npc.ts:660 and src/entities/Hotspot.ts:425.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Repro in tmp/review/framebuilder-filters-masks/inactive.test.ts. A world container has an AlphaFilter, sprite A (16x16 at 10,10) and an npc container at (200,200) holding a sprite. With npc.visible=false the filter bounds are [10,10,26,26] (same as master). With npc.setActive(false) they are [0,0,26,26]: the never-updated child adds its unit rect at identity. For an NPC that was active and then deactivated, its last-frame root-relative rect, including the old camera offset, is added instead.
confirmed.game_impact: The world filter (WorldFilterPipeline on worldContainer) is a ColorMatrixFilter loaded for scenes with filterId: test_room_a, 雾津街头, teahouse (teahouse_evening) and 码头白天. worldContainer contains NPC and hotspot containers, which are deactivated through setActive. Filter bounds, pool texture size and uInputSize/uOutputFrame differ from master whenever the stale rect lies inside the viewport but outside the visible world content. Bounds are clipped to the viewport, and ColorMatrix leaves transparent pixels transparent, so in most frames the pixels match. It is still a divergence in filter setup, and any world filter that writes color into transparent areas would show it visibly.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In fastBoundsRecursive, return early when `!c._activeSelf`, matching getLocalBounds and getGlobalBounds.

primary.reasoning:
Code: src/engine2d/gpu/FrameBuilder.ts:950-951 `fastBoundsRecursive` returns early only when `c.localDisplayStatus !== 7 || !c.measurable`, with no `_activeSelf` check. collect.ts updateChild (lines ~53-58) returns early for `!c._activeSelf` after setting globalDisplayStatus=0, so the inactive node's groupTransform and its descendants' are never refreshed. The filter-area pass (calculateFilterArea at FrameBuilder.ts:846) still descends into those nodes and adds their bounds at the stale groupTransform. Container.getLocalBounds and getGlobalBounds (Container.ts:1460, 1492) do skip `!_activeSelf`, so the renderer-side copy is the odd one out. Pixi reference getFastGlobalBoundsMixin.mjs:22-24 skips `localDisplayStatus !== 7`, which is what master's `visible=false` relied on.

Repro: .claude/review-repros/engine2d-r1/verify-framebuilder-filters-masks-0/inactive.test.ts (passes; run with --disableConsoleIntercept to see the output). Setup: a world container with an AlphaFilter, sprite A 16x16 at (10,10), and npc container at (100,100) holding a 16x16 sprite. It reads the recorded filterStack[0].bounds.
- Never-active npc: visible=false gives [10,10,26,26]; Pixi getBounds gives [10,10,26,26]; setActive(false) gives [0,0,26,26], because the child's unit rect is added at an identity groupTransform.
- Active for one frame, then setActive(false) and world moved by (-5,-5): the branch gives [5,5,116,116], Pixi/master gives [5,5,21,21]. The NPC's old rect is kept at its last-frame position and does not follow the camera move.
So the divergence in filter bounds is real.

Game path: NPC and hotspot containers are added to renderer.entityLayer (src/systems/SceneManager.ts:1479, 1558), which is a child of worldContainer (src/rendering/Renderer.ts:167-170). worldContainer gets filters through WorldFilterPipeline (Renderer.ts:79; WorldFilterPipeline.ts:21) in scenes with filterId: test_room_a/雾津街头 = day, teahouse/dev_teahouse_alive = teahouse_evening, 码头白天 = identity. Presence is set through container.setActive at src/entities/Npc.ts:660 and src/entities/Hotspot.ts:425. So the game does hit this path every frame an absent NPC or hotspot sits in a filtered scene.

Severity: lowered from medium to low. The bounds are clipped to the viewport (FrameBuilder.ts:882, clipToViewport defaults to true) and the background layer normally fills the viewport, so the final filter frame is usually identical. Even when a stale rect enlarges the frame, every shipped filter JSON (public/assets/data/filters/day.json, identity.json, teahouse_evening.json) has a zero alpha-row offset, so the ColorMatrix output stays transparent where the input is transparent. I found no pixel difference with the current content. It remains a latent divergence in filter setup: frame size and uniforms can differ, and any future world filter that writes into transparent areas, or a scene whose background does not cover the viewport together with such a filter, would show it. Other filter users (SpriteEntity pixelDensityBlur, EntityShadow castMesh blur, irradianceProbe) filter leaf nodes with no setActive children, so they are unaffected.
primary.fix_suggestion: In src/engine2d/gpu/FrameBuilder.ts fastBoundsRecursive, change the first line to `if (!c._activeSelf || c.localDisplayStatus !== 7 || !c.measurable) return;`. This matches Container.getLocalBounds and getGlobalBounds (Container.ts:1460/1492) and reproduces master's visible=false exclusion. It also avoids reading stale groupTransforms, because updateChild never refreshes inactive subtrees. Add a regression test like the repro: bounds under setActive(false) must equal bounds under visible=false, both for a never-active node and after the node is deactivated and the parent is moved.

confirmed.title: autoGenerateMipmaps is ignored: HUD flame sheet is sampled without mipmaps (outside this slice: GpuTextures)
confirmed.description: GpuTextures.get creates every texture without mipLevels, and nothing in engine2d/gpu generates mips or listens for TextureSource 'updateMipmaps'. The RHI does support mipLevels (LumaRhiDevice.ts:1026). A source with `autoGenerateMipmaps = true` therefore gets a single-level texture, and the 'linear' mipmapFilter has nothing to act on. On master (Pixi WebGL), GlTextureSystem sets mipLevelCount = floor(log2(max(w,h))) + 1 when the source is first initialised and calls gl.generateMipmap on upload (WebGL2 supports non-power-of-two mipmaps).
confirmed.reference: node_modules/pixi.js/lib/rendering/renderers/gl/texture/GlTextureSystem.mjs:147-149 (mipLevelCount from autoGenerateMipmaps), :174 (mip-aware sampler), :217-224 (generateMipmap). Master src/ui/HUD.ts:1161 is identical.
confirmed.failure_scenario: HUD.loadFlameSheet sets `tex.source.autoGenerateMipmaps = true; scaleMode = 'linear'; update()` and then shows frames at about 1/4 scale. On master this is trilinear-filtered. On the branch it is bilinear on a single level at 4x minification, so fine lines alias and shimmer while the flames animate. The code comment names exactly this symptom: 不然细刻线一动就闪.
confirmed.game_impact: src/ui/HUD.ts:1161-1163: the three HUD flame sprites, always on screen. This is the only game user of autoGenerateMipmaps. It is outside the framebuilder slice and should be checked by whoever owns textures/GpuTextures.
confirmed.suggested_fix: When source.autoGenerateMipmaps is set, create the RHI texture with mipLevels = floor(log2(max(pw,ph))) + 1, generate the mips after upload (blit chain), and recreate the texture if the flag changes after the GPU texture already exists.

primary.reasoning:
I reproduced this with NullRhiDevice and WebGPURenderer, following HUD.loadFlameSheet step by step. The test uses a 588x612 BufferImageSource, the same size as the 12x6 grid of 49x102 frames. It sets `autoGenerateMipmaps = true`, then `scaleMode = 'linear'`, then calls `update()`, and draws a Sprite with a 49x102 frame at scale 0.25.

What the branch records:
- One texture is created for the sheet as `{w:588,h:612}` with no mipLevels, so it has 1 level.
- The sampler has minFilter, magFilter and mipmapFilter all set to 'linear'.
- `writeTexture` is called once. `source.mipLevelCount` stays 1 and 'updateMipmaps' is never emitted.
- No other code in src/engine2d/gpu reads autoGenerateMipmaps or mipLevelCount. The only mipmap reference there is the sampler's mipmapFilter at GpuTextures.ts:108. Texture creation at GpuTextures.ts:67-73 never passes mipLevels.

Master behaviour:
- master's Renderer.ts:138 calls `app.init` with no `preference`, so it runs Pixi 8's default WebGL renderer.
- GlTextureSystem._initSource (node_modules/pixi.js/lib/rendering/renderers/gl/texture/GlTextureSystem.mjs:147-149) sets `mipLevelCount = floor(log2(max(w,h))) + 1` when `autoGenerateMipmaps` is set. For this sheet that is 10 levels, since WebGL2 allows non-power-of-two mipmaps.
- updateStyle (:174) passes `mipmaps = mipLevelCount > 1` to applyStyleParams, which gives LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR.
- onSourceUpdate (:217-219) calls `gl.generateMipmap` after upload.
- HUD sets the flag right after `Assets.load` and before the first render, so on master `_initSource` sees `autoGenerateMipmaps = true` and the sheet is sampled trilinearly.
- The branch instead samples one 588x612 level bilinearly at about 4x minification. Fine lines alias and shimmer as the frames animate, which is the symptom the HUD comment (不然细刻线一动就闪) says the flag is there to prevent.

Game impact:
- The divergent path is src/ui/HUD.ts:1161-1163 (identical on master). It is the only game code that sets autoGenerateMipmaps; the engine2d text code passes it through but defaults to false. It affects the three HUD flame sprites, which are always visible once the sheet (ui/three_fires_sheet.png under the external media root) loads. If the file is missing, the HUD falls back to the vector flames and this path is not used.

Severity: medium. The output is still correct and nothing crashes; the difference is filtering quality (aliasing and shimmer) on an always-visible HUD element. It could be argued up to high because it is visible, but the image is not wrong in content.
primary.fix_suggestion:
In GpuTextures.get (src/engine2d/gpu/GpuTextures.ts:62-86):
1. When `source.autoGenerateMipmaps` is true, compute `levels = Math.floor(Math.log2(Math.max(source.width, source.height))) + 1`, matching Pixi GL `_initSource`. Write it back to `source.mipLevelCount`, the same way Pixi mutates the source. Pass `mipLevels: levels` to `scope.createTexture`. RENDER_TARGET usage is already present for image sources; it is also needed for blit-based generation.
2. Store `mipLevels` in the Entry. If a later `get` finds that `source.autoGenerateMipmaps` no longer matches it, recreate the texture, as the existing resourceId check already does.
3. After `upload()`, when `autoGenerateMipmaps && levels > 1`, generate the mip chain on the GPU. WebGPU has no generateMipmap, so render each level from the previous one with a linear-filtered blit, one render pass per level.
4. Subscribe to the source's 'updateMipmaps' event to regenerate, and unsubscribe in `release`.
5. Add a NullRhiDevice test asserting `mipLevels === 10` and that the sampler uses mipmapFilter 'linear' for the 588x612 HUD case.

confirmed.title: popMaskEnd restores INVERSE stencil mode after popping an inverse mask; Pixi restores MASK_ACTIVE
confirmed.description: collect.ts:231 copies effect.inverse into the popMaskEnd instruction, and maskExecute then does `setStencilMode(instr.inverse ? 'inverse' : 'active', maskStackIndex)`. Pixi's popMaskEnd instruction carries no inverse field (StencilMaskPipe.pop), so execute always sets MASK_ACTIVE with the decremented index. After a top-level inverse mask is popped, the stencil is back to 0 everywhere. The branch then leaves the target in compare 'not-equal', ref 0, so every later draw on that target fails the stencil test until the next mask instruction. For a nested case (inverse inner mask inside a normal outer mask) the branch selects 'inverse' ref 1, which draws outside the outer mask. Related: setMask keeps `inverse` on the MaskEffect (Container.ts:1251-1254), so it is lost when the mask object changes and ignored when set before a mask exists. Pixi keeps it in container._maskOptions (effectsMixin.mjs:48-54).

primary.reasoning:
I ran a repro that puts the two implementations side by side. On the engine2d side, WebGPURenderer runs on NullRhiDevice and I read the stencil mode of each recorded draw. On the Pixi side, I built instructions with Pixi's real StencilMaskPipe.push/pop (node_modules/pixi.js/lib/rendering/mask/stencil/StencilMaskPipe.mjs) and fed them to its execute() through a mock renderer that records setStencilMode calls.

Top-level case: a Graphics mask, a sprite with setMask({mask, inverse:true}), then a sibling sprite.
- engine2d draws: add/0, inverse/1, remove/1, inverse/0. The draw after the pop uses the 'inverse' pipeline, which Pipelines.ts:31 defines as compare not-equal, with ref 0.
- Pixi: the popMaskEnd instruction has inverse=undefined, because StencilMaskPipe.mjs:66-70 adds no inverse field. execute (:101-107) therefore sets MASK_ACTIVE/0, which is compare equal, ref 0.

Nested case: an inverse inner mask inside a normal outer mask.
- engine2d restores inverse/1 after the inner pop. Pixi restores MASK_ACTIVE/1.
- So a sibling of the inner masked sprite, still inside the outer mask, draws outside the outer mask on the branch and inside it on Pixi.

The secondary claim also holds. Container.ts:1251-1254 applies inverse only if a _maskEffect already exists. The flag lives on the MaskEffect, so it is lost when the mask changes (a new MaskEffect is created with inverse=false). Pixi keeps it in container._maskOptions.

Then read it in collect.pushMask/popMask from the container instead of from the MaskEffect.

confirmed.title: FilterEffect.priority is 0 (Pixi uses 1), so the order of filter and mask on one container depends on assignment order
confirmed.description: Pixi sorts container.effects by priority: mask effects are 0 and FilterEffect is 1, so a mask is always the outer effect and filters the inner one. On the branch both are 0, and the stable sort keeps insertion order. If `filters` is set before `mask`, the collector emits pushFilter, then pushMask, and so on. The mask is then drawn into the filter's input texture and the filter output reaches the target without stencil clipping, so blur or padding spill shows outside the mask. Pixi instead clips the filtered result with the canvas stencil.
confirmed.reference: node_modules/pixi.js/lib/filters/FilterEffect.mjs:7 (`this.priority = 1`), rendering/mask/stencil/StencilMask.mjs:9 (priority 0), scene/container/container-mixins/effectsMixin.mjs:22 (sort by priority).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Repro in tmp/review/framebuilder-filters-masks/masks.test.ts. c.filters = [f]; c.mask = g. engine2d effects are ['filters', 'mask']; Pixi effects are ['stencilMask', 'filter'].
confirmed.game_impact: No game container carries both a mask and filters. The masked containers (UIScrollView.content, InventoryUI nameText, DevModeUI contentContainer, DialogueUI bodyText, ObjectExamineScene viewLayer) never get filters, and the filtered ones have no mask. Latent only.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Set `priority = 1` on FilterEffect.

primary.reasoning:
Code evidence: src/engine2d/scene/Container.ts:133 sets `FilterEffect.priority = 0`, and MaskEffect (Container.ts:96) is also 0. Container.addEffect (Container.ts:1281-1282) pushes the effect and then runs a stable sort by priority, so with equal priorities the order is just assignment order. In Pixi 8.17, node_modules/pixi.js/lib/filters/FilterEffect.mjs:7 sets priority = 1, and StencilMask, AlphaMask, ColorMask and ScissorMask all use 0. effectsMixin.mjs:22 sorts by priority, so a mask is always the outer effect. The collector (src/engine2d/gpu/collect.ts:167-182) pushes effects in array order and pops them in reverse, so effects[0] is the outermost.

Repro, run with vitest on NullRhiDevice plus the 'pixi.js' Container:
- engine2d, filters set then mask: effects ['filters','mask'], instructions [pushFilter, pushMaskBegin, pushMaskEnd, popMaskBegin, popMaskEnd, popFilter].
- engine2d, mask set then filters: effects ['mask','filters'], instructions [pushMaskBegin, pushMaskEnd, pushFilter, popFilter, popMaskBegin, popMaskEnd].
- Pixi, either order: ['StencilMask:0','FilterEffect:1'].

So on the branch, `c.filters = [...]` followed by `c.mask = g` puts the stencil inside the filter pass. The filter output is then composited without the mask clip, so blur or padding spill shows outside the mask, where Pixi clips it.

Game impact: I found none. I grepped every game-side `.mask =`, `setMask(`, `.filters =` and `addEffect` under src (excluding engine2d and tests, and including src/rendering).
- Masked containers: UIScrollView.content (UIScrollView.ts:93/160), InventoryUI nameText (InventoryUI.ts:465), DevModeUI contentContainer (DevModeUI.ts:290 and after), DialogueUI bodyText (DialogueUI.ts:811), ObjectExamineScene viewLayer (ObjectExamineScene.ts:401).
- Filtered containers: DepthDebugVisualizer backgroundLayer, WaterMinigame sprites, ObjectExamine bgSprite and objectRoot, SceneManager/Game NPC and player containers, Hotspot displaySprite, SceneDepthSystem, SpriteEntity sprite (SpriteEntity.ts:1667).

The two sets do not overlap, so no container gets both effects. The issue is latent, and low severity is correct.
primary.fix_suggestion: In src/engine2d/scene/Container.ts:133, change `priority = 0;` to `priority = 1;` on FilterEffect, as Pixi's FilterEffect.mjs:7 does. Leave MaskEffect at 0. addEffect already runs a stable sort by priority, so the mask becomes effects[0], which is the outer push and the last pop, whatever the assignment order. Add a regression test that sets filters before mask and expects the effect kinds to be ['mask','filters'] and the collector to emit pushMask before pushFilter.

confirmed.title: Sprite masks (and number or color masks) are always treated as stencil masks
confirmed.description: Collector.pushMask always emits stencil instructions and FrameBuilder only implements the stencil pipe. Pixi picks AlphaMask when the mask is a Sprite (a MaskFilter applied through the filter system, which respects texture alpha and channel) and ColorMask when it is a number. On the branch a Sprite mask clips to its full quad, because every fragment increments the stencil regardless of alpha, and a numeric mask is not supported.
confirmed.reference: node_modules/pixi.js/lib/rendering/mask/alpha/AlphaMask.mjs:43-45 (`mask instanceof Sprite`) and rendering/mask/color/ColorMask.mjs:17-19.
confirmed.failure_scenario: container.mask = new Sprite(circleTexture): Pixi shows only the circle's alpha region; the branch shows the whole rectangular sprite quad.
confirmed.game_impact: None today: every game mask is a Graphics (UIScrollView.ts:86, InventoryUI.ts:461, DevModeUI.ts:284 and later, DialogueUI bodyMask, ObjectExamineScene.ts:228). Latent only.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Either implement the alpha-mask path, or throw or warn when a Sprite is assigned as a mask so the divergence cannot happen silently.

primary.reasoning:
I ran the repro with `npx vitest run ... --silent=false`.

**Pixi 8.17 side.** I read `container.effects` after setting a mask:
- A Sprite mask gives `AlphaMask/alphaMask`.
- A number mask gives `ColorMask/colorMask`.
- A Graphics mask gives `StencilMask/stencilMask`.

This matches `node_modules/pixi.js/lib/rendering/mask/alpha/AlphaMask.mjs:43-45` (`mask instanceof Sprite`) and `color/ColorMask.mjs:17-19` (`typeof mask === 'number'`).

**engine2d side.**
- The `mask` setter in `src/engine2d/scene/Container.ts:1238-1249` always creates the one generic `MaskEffect` (`Container.ts:94`), whatever the mask is.
- `Collector.pushMask` (`src/engine2d/gpu/collect.ts:211-224`) always emits `pushMaskBegin`/`pushMaskEnd`. `FrameBuilder.maskExecute` (`FrameBuilder.ts:625-648`) turns those into stencil add, active and remove modes only.
- I rendered a Sprite(Texture.WHITE) mask on NullRhiDevice. The recorded commands are `drawIndexed engine2d-batch -> bgra8unorm+add`, then `+active`, then `+remove`. That is stencil-only, with no alpha-mask filter pass.
- There is no `discard` anywhere in `src/engine2d/gpu/`. Every fragment of the mask sprite's quad increments the stencil, so texture alpha is ignored. A circular-alpha sprite mask clips to its full rectangle on the branch; Pixi clips to the circle.
- A numeric mask (`c.mask = 0xff0000`) is worse than "not supported": it throws `TypeError: Cannot create property 'includeInBuild' on number` in the MaskEffect constructor (`Container.ts:99-100`). Pixi accepts it silently as a ColorMask.

**Game impact: none.** Every `.mask =` assignment in game code outside engine2d uses a Graphics or null:
- `UIScrollView.ts:93/160/441` (maskG is a Graphics, `UIScrollView.ts:86`)
- `InventoryUI.ts:465` (nameMask is a Graphics, `InventoryUI.ts:461`)
- `DevModeUI.ts:290/384/424/469/510` (contentMask is a Graphics, `DevModeUI.ts:284/378`)
- `DialogueUI.ts:811` (bodyMask)
- `ObjectExamineScene.ts:401/758` (viewMask)

No game code calls `setMask(`. Graphics masks take the stencil path in both Pixi and the branch, so the game never reaches the divergent path. This is a latent API gap, so severity stays low.
primary.fix_suggestion:
Smallest change consistent with Pixi's mask selection: in the `set mask` setter (`src/engine2d/scene/Container.ts:1238`), fail loudly for the mask kinds engine2d does not implement instead of silently using stencil:
- `if (typeof value === 'number') throw new Error('engine2d: ColorMask (numeric mask) not supported')`
- `if (value instanceof Sprite) throw new Error('engine2d: AlphaMask (Sprite mask) not supported; use a Graphics mask')`

To avoid a circular import, check a duck-typed flag or the Sprite class via a late import.

A full implementation would port Pixi's `AlphaMaskPipe`: render the mask into a RenderTexture sized to the mask bounds and apply a MaskFilter through the filter stack, using the sprite texture's alpha (and channel). It would also need the `ColorMaskPipe` (per-channel color write mask). Neither is needed by the game today.
