confirmed.title: GPU buffers are never freed unless Buffer.destroy() is called; master's Pixi GC reclaims them. This leaks per scene load, per burn and per breathing overlay
confirmed.description: GpuBuffers holds a strong Map<Buffer, Entry> and releases an entry only on the Buffer's 'destroy' event. There is no GC system in the branch (grep: no GCSystem or _gcLastUsed). Mesh.destroy() does not destroy the geometry, and Geometry.destroy() defaults to destroyBuffers=false. Any mesh torn down as mesh.destroy() or geometry.destroy() therefore keeps its RHI vertex and index buffers, plus the CPU Buffer objects and their typed arrays, until the renderer is destroyed. Repro (tmp/review/renderer-resources/res.test.ts): 5 cycles of creating a custom-shader Mesh with a MeshGeometry, rendering it, then mesh.destroy() + geometry.destroy() + shader.destroy() leave 15 of 15 geometry RHI buffers alive.
confirmed.reference: Master (Pixi 8.17 WebGL): node_modules/pixi.js/lib/rendering/renderers/gl/buffer/GlBufferSystem.mjs:19-24 registers buffers in a GCManagedHash, and :40 stamps _gcLastUsed on every use. node_modules/pixi.js/lib/rendering/renderers/shared/GCSystem.mjs:298-305 (gcActive, 60s unused, runs every 30s) and :runOnHash call resource.unload(), which frees the GL buffer and drops the reference (Buffer.autoGarbageCollect = true, shared/buffer/Buffer.mjs:34). GpuTextures.ts:42/77 has the same shape for textures (strong map, freed only on destroy/unload, no idle GC).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Each scene load runs SceneLightingSystem.load, which constructs SceneLightingPass (+ShadowPrefixPass), LitBackground, optionally GiBouncePass, and passPlate, each a MeshGeometry quad. On unload they call only this.mesh.destroy(): SceneLightingPass.ts:1642, LitBackground.ts:368, GiBouncePass.ts:256, shadowPrefix.ts:465. That leaves about 3 RHI buffers per mesh, roughly 12-15 per scene switch, permanently. BurnRenderer.ts:448 (e.geometry?.destroy()) and breathingOverlayMesh.ts:159 (geometry.destroy()) leak 3 buffers per burn effect and per breathing-overlay show. Master frees all of these about 60s after last use.
confirmed.game_impact: GPU buffer count and pinned JS objects grow without bound over a play session (scene switches, burns, cutscene breathing overlays). Each allocation is small (quad-sized), so this is a slow leak rather than a crash. Texture memory is mostly bounded, because the game unloads through the AssetManager budget and CharacterLightingSystem/SceneLightingSystem destroy their own BufferImageSources.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Also release on the Geometry's 'destroy' event for buffers owned by that geometry only, or add an idle-GC pass over the GpuBuffers/GpuTextures entries that mirrors Pixi (stamp last-used per render, unload after N ms, skip autoGarbageCollect=false). Alternatively, make the game call geometry.destroy(true) at the sites listed above.

primary.reasoning:
Repro: .claude/review-repros/engine2d-r1/verify-renderer-resources-1/gc.test.ts. All 3 tests pass.
(1) engine2d on NullRhiDevice, following the game's pattern: 5 cycles of creating a custom-shader Mesh with a MeshGeometry quad, rendering it, then mesh.destroy(), geometry.destroy() and shader.destroy(). After that the test renders an empty stage for another 120 simulated seconds, with performance.now mocked. Result: 15 of 15 geometry RHI buffers are still alive (position, uv and index buffer for each cycle).
(2) With geometry.destroy(true), 0 buffers are alive. So the release path works; it just never runs for the game's teardown pattern.
(3) Pixi 8.17 side, which is what master runs, using the real GCSystem and GCManagedHash exported from 'pixi.js': a Buffer added to the hash the way GlBufferSystem.createGLBuffer adds it has autoGarbageCollect = true. It survives a GC run at 30s. At 70s its gpuData.destroy() is called and the hash slot is nulled.

Code evidence:
- src/engine2d/gpu/GpuBuffers.ts:24 holds a strong Map<Buffer, Entry>. Line 51 is the only release trigger, `buffer.once('destroy', ...)`, besides the resourceId change and renderer.destroy.
- The branch has no GC system. grep finds `_gcLastUsed` only in GraphicsContext. engine2d Buffer has no autoGarbageCollect and no unload path.
- src/engine2d/shader/Geometry.ts:164-168: destroy(destroyBuffers = false) destroys the buffers only when the flag is set.
- src/engine2d/mesh/Mesh.ts:171 does not destroy the geometry. This matches Pixi Mesh.mjs:175.
- Master: node_modules/pixi.js/lib/rendering/renderers/gl/buffer/GlBufferSystem.mjs:19-24 creates a GCManagedHash, and :40 stamps _gcLastUsed on each use. GCSystem.mjs:226-270 (runOnHash) unloads entries that are older than gcMaxUnusedTime and have autoGarbageCollect set. The defaults at :298-304 are gcActive true, 60s and 30s. Master's src never overrides gcActive (grep finds nothing).
- The game code is identical on master. For example, master EntityShadow.ts:848/851 and LitBackground.ts:231 do the same thing. So on master these buffers were reclaimed about 60-90s after last use; on the branch they live until renderer.destroy().

Game call sites that hit the path (all custom-shader meshes, so their buffers go through GpuBuffers):
- Every scene load / entity:
  - src/rendering/CharacterLitSprite.ts:1259 (LitSpriteQuad.destroy calls only mesh.destroy(); the comment wrongly says "含 geometry"). It is created per SpriteEntity at SpriteEntity.ts:568/1312 and destroyed at :531/549/1323. That is about 4 buffers: positions, uvs, aLocal, index.
  - src/rendering/EntityShadow.ts:1286-1291 (PlanarEntityShadow; castGeometry.destroy() and contactGeometry.destroy() without true). It is created per NPC/hotspot at Game.ts:7146. That is 6 buffers.
  - SceneLightingPass.ts:1642, shadowPrefix.ts:465, LitBackground.ts:368 and GiBouncePass.ts:256, created from SceneLightingSystem.ts:282/515/529/732. That is about 3 buffers per mesh.
- Per effect / cutscene:
  - BurnRenderer.ts:448
  - breathingOverlayMesh.ts:159 (via BreathingOverlaySystem.ts:82)
  - overlayBlendShader.ts:175 (via CutsceneRenderer.ts:1628)
- Not affected: backgroundSway and the Vfx*Mesh classes already call destroy(true).

So a scene switch with N shadowed characters leaks roughly 10N + 12-15 small RHI buffers, plus their CPU Buffer, typed-array and Geometry objects, which stay reachable through the Map and the buffers' update listeners. The count grows without bound over a session.

Severity: the growth is per scene, but each buffer is quad-sized (tens of bytes, likely a small allocation granule on WebGPU). The per-scene total is on the order of 100 tiny buffers, with no frame breakage or crash in realistic sessions. So this fits "small leak" = medium. You could argue for high or critical under the literal "grows per scene" rule, but the absolute memory is negligible. GpuTextures has the same shape; I did not verify it here.

Checked and equivalent: Mesh.destroy not destroying the geometry, and Geometry.destroy defaulting to not destroying buffers, both match Pixi 8.17. The divergence is only the missing idle GC.
primary.fix_suggestion:
The fix should match Pixi's behaviour. It should not rely only on callers.

1. Add `autoGarbageCollect = true` and `_gcLastUsed = -1` to engine2d Buffer (src/engine2d/shader/Buffer.ts).
2. In GpuBuffers.get(), stamp `buffer._gcLastUsed = renderer.gcNow`, where gcNow is set to performance.now() at the start of each render.
3. Add a `collect(now, maxUnused = 60000)` method to GpuBuffers. For each entry with `buffer.autoGarbageCollect && now - buffer._gcLastUsed >= maxUnused`, call `this.release(buffer)`, which destroys the RHI buffer and deletes the map entry. If the Buffer is used again, get() recreates it and re-uploads it (updateId -1), so this is safe for buffers shared by several geometries.
4. In WebGPURenderer postrender, call collect when at least 30000 ms have passed since the last collect. Expose gcActive, gcMaxUnusedTime and gcFrequency options with Pixi's defaults: true, 60000, 30000.
5. Also make release() remove its 'destroy' listener, or guard it, so recreating an entry does not pile up once-listeners.

The same pattern can be applied to GpuTextures for sources with autoGarbageCollect set.

Also fix the teardown sites with geometry.destroy(true) (or destroy the mesh's geometry with buffers):
- CharacterLitSprite.ts:1259
- EntityShadow.ts:1288/1291
- SceneLightingPass.ts:1642
- shadowPrefix.ts:465
- LitBackground.ts:368
- GiBouncePass.ts:256
- BurnRenderer.ts:448
- breathingOverlayMesh.ts:159
- overlayBlendShader.ts:175

This frees the buffers immediately. Without the GC, other unlisted paths would still leak.

confirmed.title: Device loss is permanent: the renderer never recovers, while master's WebGL context restores and re-uploads
confirmed.description: After luma.lost resolves (LumaRhiDevice.ts:928-933 only sets _isLost and reports it), runFrame and submit return false immediately (:1214, :1271). WebGPURenderer.render ignores the return value (WebGPURenderer.ts:216-217). Nothing in engine2d, createRenderer or the game re-requests an adapter/device or rebuilds GpuTextures/GpuBuffers/Pipelines. The canvas stops updating for good.
confirmed.reference: node_modules/pixi.js/lib/rendering/renderers/gl/context/GlContextSystem.mjs:103-104 and :176-191 (handleContextLost calls event.preventDefault() so the browser will restore; handleContextRestored emits contextChange). GlTextureSystem.mjs:53-61 (contextChange -> _managedTextures.removeAll(true), so textures re-upload lazily from their CPU resources) and GlBufferSystem contextChange -> destroyAll(true). Master Game.ts:4603-4610 only logs webglcontextlost/restored and relies on Pixi to recover.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A GPU process crash, driver update or reset, Windows TDR, or GPU switch on a laptop loses the device. Master: Pixi prevents the default, the context is restored, and resource-backed textures and buffers re-upload, so the game keeps running (per-frame RTs are re-rendered). Branch: rhi.isLost is true, every later render is dropped, and the player sees a frozen frame until a full page reload.
confirmed.game_impact: Every scene is affected in the rare device-loss case. src/debug/gpuPanelDiagnostics.ts only surfaces the error; no game code handles recovery.
confirmed.suggested_fix: On rhi.lost, recreate the device and renderer-side caches (drop GpuTextures/GpuBuffers/Pipelines entries so they rebuild lazily from CPU sources), or at minimum surface a reload prompt.

primary.reasoning:
Code evidence. In src/rendering/rhi/backends/luma/LumaRhiDevice.ts:928-933, the constructor's `luma.lost.then(...)` does only three things: it sets `_isLost = true`, reports an RhiError('backend', '图形设备丢失…') and returns the reason. After that, `runFrame` (:1214) and `submit` (:1271) return false straight away with `if (this._isLost || this._destroyed) return false;`. WebGPURenderer.render (src/engine2d/gpu/WebGPURenderer.ts:216-217) calls `this.rhi.runFrame(...)` or `this.rhi.submit(...)` and ignores the boolean. Nothing ever clears `_isLost`. grep across src/ finds no consumer of `rhi.lost` or `isLost` outside the RHI itself (only the RhiDevice.ts interface and NullRhiDevice). The only code that creates a device is createLumaRhiDevice (LumaRhiDevice.ts:96-126), which runs once at startup. There is no re-request of adapter or device and no step that drops engine2d's GpuTexture, GpuBuffer or pipeline caches. src/debug/gpuPanelDiagnostics.ts only logs the diagnostic to the debug panel.

Reference. Pixi 8.17 GlContextSystem.mjs:103-104 registers webglcontextlost and webglcontextrestored listeners. At :176-191, handleContextLost calls event.preventDefault(), which lets the browser restore the context. handleContextRestored then emits runners.contextChange, and GlTextureSystem.mjs:53-61 responds with _managedTextures.removeAll(true), so textures re-upload lazily from their CPU sources. GL buffers and shaders are rebuilt the same way. Master's Renderer.ts:138 uses the default Pixi Application on WebGL, and master's Game.ts:4601-4611 only logs the lost and restored events, relying on Pixi to recover.

Repro: .claude/review-repros/engine2d-r1/verify-renderer-resources-2/deviceLost.test.ts, which passes. It builds a real LumaRhiDevice on a minimal fake luma Device and resolves `luma.lost`. Afterwards `dev.lost` resolves with the reason and `isLost` is true. Five `runFrame` calls and five `submit` calls all return false, and none of their record callbacks is invoked. `isLost` is still true 50 ms later. So once the device is lost, every render from engine2d is dropped silently and the canvas freezes on its last frame until a page reload.

The repro cannot run master's Pixi recovery side by side, because that needs a real WebGL context-loss and restore cycle in a browser. The Pixi code path above is unambiguous, though.

Game impact. Every scene draws through WebGPURenderer.render → rhi.runFrame, so any device loss freezes the whole game. Causes include a GPU process crash, a driver reset or TDR, a GPU switch, or the browser reclaiming the device. Master would recover in the same situation: the scene re-renders every frame, and textures re-upload from their sources. Any one-off baked RenderTextures would come back blank on master too, so master's recovery is not perfect, but it keeps the game playable.

Severity. Medium is right: the result is a full freeze, but device loss is rare and has an external cause.
primary.fix_suggestion:
Match Pixi's contextChange recovery.

- In the engine2d renderer or createRenderer, subscribe to `rhi.lost`. When it resolves, if the device was not destroyed on purpose, call createLumaRhiDevice again on the same canvas.
- Swap the new device into WebGPURenderer.
- Clear every cache that holds GPU objects from the old device: GpuTexture entries per TextureSource, GpuBuffers, the pipeline/bind-group caches, stencil targets and MSAA targets. This is the WebGPU equivalent of GlTextureSystem.contextChange → `_managedTextures.removeAll(true)` and GlBufferSystem's destroyAll(true). Resource-backed textures then re-upload lazily from their CPU sources on next use, and per-frame RenderTextures get re-rendered.
- Re-run anything that created device-bound resources outside engine2d, such as RHI scopes for lighting or bakes, or have those paths re-create lazily.

If full recovery is too much work for now, the minimal parity-preserving fallback is: on `rhi.lost`, show a blocking "graphics device lost, reload" prompt, or call `location.reload()`, instead of leaving a silently frozen frame.

confirmed.title: GPU caches add a new 'unload'/'destroy' listener every time an entry is recreated and never remove the old ones
confirmed.description: Each time GpuTextures.get creates an entry it adds source.once('destroy', ...) and source.on('unload', ...). An entry is recreated after every resize (the _resourceId change at :56-60) and after every unload and reuse, but neither the resourceId path nor release() removes the earlier listeners. GpuBuffers.ts:198 does the same with buffer.once('destroy') on every size growth. Repro: 10 resize+render cycles of one RenderTexture leave 10 'unload' and 10 'destroy' listeners on rt.source.
confirmed.reference: Pixi GCManagedHash.add (node_modules/pixi.js/lib/utils/data/GCManagedHash.mjs:17-22) is a no-op when the item is already tracked and uses item.once('unload'). GlTextureSystem.onSourceUnload (GlTextureSystem.mjs:183-194) removes its listeners.
confirmed.failure_scenario: WaterMinigameScene.ts:308-311 resizes bottomMrt/paramsMrt on every viewport change. AssetManager.disposeValue (AssetManager.ts:262) unloads an evicted texture, and when Assets.load later returns the cached Texture it is recreated. Each cycle adds 2 closures to the source.
confirmed.game_impact: Listeners grow slowly with resizes and with evict-then-reuse cycles. There is no visual effect.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Register the listeners once per source (for example track them in a WeakSet) or remove them in release() and on the resourceId-change path.

primary.reasoning:
Code: src/engine2d/gpu/GpuTextures.ts:74-78 calls `source.once('destroy', ...)` and `source.on('unload', ...)` every time an entry is created. Entries are dropped and rebuilt without removing those listeners in three places: the _resourceId-change path (:56-60, triggered by TextureSource.resize at TextureSource.ts:207 and unload at :168), the sampled-to-render-target upgrade (:80-84, which recurses into get), and release() (:113-119, which runs on unload). GpuBuffers.ts:51 does the same with `buffer.once('destroy', ...)` whenever Buffer._resourceId changes (Buffer.ts:90, when the data length changes). Pixi 8.17 avoids this. GpuTextureSystem._initSource (GpuTextureSystem.mjs:91-96) registers update/resize/updateMipmaps only when GCManagedHash.add returns true, and add is a no-op for an item it already tracks (GCManagedHash.mjs:17-22, using once('unload')). onSourceUnload (:117-120) removes the listeners, and a resize rebuilds the GPU texture without adding listeners.

Repro (NullRhiDevice + WebGPURenderer, vitest, output checked with --reporter=verbose):
- RenderTexture 8x8: 10 rounds of resize then render took 'unload'/'destroy' listeners from [0,0] to [10,10].
- Sampled TextureSource: 10 rounds of render then unload left unload=10 and destroy=10 listeners. After 10 more ordinary frames the count was 11/11, so steady rendering does not add listeners; they grow only when an entry is rebuilt.
- After source.destroy() both counts were 0/0, because TextureSource.destroy calls removeAllListeners.

The growth is therefore limited to live sources and to the number of resize or unload-and-reuse events, and it does not grow per frame. Every extra handler just calls release(source) again, which does nothing once the entry is gone, so there is no functional or visual difference.

Game call sites:
- src/systems/waterMinigame/WaterMinigameScene.ts:308/311 resizes bottomMrt/paramsMrt only when the computed texture size changes (viewport change).
- src/core/AssetManager.ts:262 disposeValue calls `source.unload()` on evicted textures (evict at :244, plus :187/:556/:582). If the same Texture object is drawn again, it gains another pair of listeners.
- Buffer growth: no game code reassigns Buffer.data. It only happens through the MeshGeometry setters in engine2d (MeshGeometry.ts:48-62/116-118).

This is a slow, bounded closure build-up with no effect on output. It is a divergence from Pixi's listener hygiene but not a meaningful leak. Severity stays low.
primary.fix_suggestion: In GpuTextures, register the source hooks only once per source, as Pixi's GCManagedHash.add does. Add `private readonly hooked = new WeakSet<TextureSource>();` and wrap lines 77-78 as `if (!this.hooked.has(source)) { this.hooked.add(source); source.once('destroy', () => this.release(source)); source.on('unload', () => this.release(source)); }`. The persistent 'unload' handler keeps working across rebuilds, and destroy() clears everything through removeAllListeners. An equivalent Pixi-style option: use one bound handler `private readonly onGone = (s: TextureSource) => this.release(s)`, and in release() and the two delete paths (:56-60 and :80-84) call `source.off('unload', this.onGone); source.off('destroy', this.onGone)` before re-adding. Apply the same WeakSet guard around `buffer.once('destroy', ...)` in GpuBuffers.ts:51.

confirmed.title: extract.* un-premultiplies pixels, but master (Pixi WebGL) returns them premultiplied; also extract.base64 'jpg' gives an invalid MIME type
confirmed.description: readPixels divides r/g/b by a for 0<a<255. Master's WebGL getPixels does not: its unpremultiply call is dead code. So extract.pixels/canvas/base64 output differs from master on every semi-transparent pixel. Separately, base64 calls c.toDataURL(`image/${format}`), so format 'jpg' becomes 'image/jpg'. Browsers do not recognise that and silently fall back to PNG. Pixi maps jpg to 'image/jpeg' (ExtractSystem.mjs imageTypes) and defaults quality to 1.
confirmed.reference: node_modules/pixi.js/lib/rendering/renderers/gl/texture/GlTextureSystem.mjs:379-402 (readPixels, then `if (false) { unpremultiplyAlpha(pixels) }`). node_modules/pixi.js/lib/rendering/renderers/shared/extract/ExtractSystem.mjs imageTypes {jpg:'image/jpeg'} and defaultImageOptions {format:'png', quality:1}.
confirmed.failure_scenario: extract.base64({target: app.stage, frame, resolution: 2}) over an anti-aliased or half-transparent UI edge with clearColor [0,0,0,0]. Master writes premultiplied bytes into the canvas; the branch writes straight-alpha bytes, so those pixels come out brighter than master's.
confirmed.game_impact: The only game caller is the dev UI screenshot harness (src/dev/uiShotHarness.ts:184, png). Runtime gameplay does not use extract. Screenshots compared against master-captured baselines would differ at alpha edges.
confirmed.suggested_fix: If the goal is master parity, skip the un-premultiply step. Map format through {png:'image/png', jpg:'image/jpeg', webp:'image/webp'} and default quality to 1.

primary.reasoning:
I reproduced both parts in node. The repro runs a real engine2d WebGPURenderer on a NullRhiDevice, with rhi.readTexture stubbed to return the same premultiplied GPU bytes that a fake gl.readPixels hands to Pixi 8.17's real GlTextureSystem.prototype.getPixels. Input bytes: [64,64,64,128 | 200,100,50,255 | 0,0,0,0 | 10,20,30,40].
- Pixi WebGL returns the bytes unchanged: [64,64,64,128, 200,100,50,255, 0,0,0,0, 10,20,30,40]. In node_modules/pixi.js/lib/rendering/renderers/gl/texture/GlTextureSystem.mjs:379-402 the unpremultiplyAlpha call is guarded by `if (false)`.
- engine2d returns [128,128,128,128, 200,100,50,255, 0,0,0,0, 64,128,191,40]. The cause is src/engine2d/gpu/WebGPURenderer.ts:465-469 (readPixels divides by a when 0<a<255).
So every semi-transparent pixel from extract.pixels/canvas/base64/image comes out brighter than master's. Opaque and fully transparent pixels match.

Master is on WebGL: master src/rendering/Renderer.ts:138 calls app.init with no `preference`, and Pixi 8.17's autoDetectRenderer tries renderPriority ['webgl','webgpu','canvas'] in that order. So the WebGL getPixels path is the right reference.

MIME part: extract.base64({format:'jpg'}) calls toDataURL('image/jpg', undefined), which the repro recorded (src/engine2d/gpu/WebGPURenderer.ts:540-541). Pixi maps it through imageTypes {jpg:'image/jpeg'} and defaults quality to 1 (ExtractSystem.mjs:7-11, 101-120, 383-385). Browsers do not recognise 'image/jpg' and fall back to PNG. For JPEG, quality undefined means the browser default (about 0.92) instead of 1.

Game impact: the only caller is the DEV-only UI screenshot harness, src/dev/uiShotHarness.ts:184, installed from src/core/Game.ts:2165 under import.meta.env.DEV. It calls extract.base64({target: app.stage, format:'png', frame, resolution: 2}). Consequences:
- It uses png, so the jpg MIME bug is never hit by the game.
- The un-premultiply divergence only shows at pixels the stage leaves partially transparent. generateTexture clears to [0,0,0,0] and does not include the app background. Opaque scene backgrounds cover most shots.
- Runtime gameplay never uses extract.

So this is a real parity divergence, confined to a dev tool. Severity: low.

confirmed.title: HTMLVideoElement sources never upload (the width===0 guard reads the video's layout width attribute)
confirmed.description: upload() returns early when resource.width === 0 to skip unloaded images. For an HTMLVideoElement, .width is the HTML width attribute (0 by default), not videoWidth. ImageSource accepts HTMLVideoElement (TextureSource.ts:244) and resourceWidth reads videoWidth, so the GPU texture is created at the right size but never filled.
confirmed.reference: Pixi uploads video via glUploadVideoResource/glUploadImageResource using resourceWidth (node_modules/pixi.js/lib/rendering/renderers/gl/texture/uploaders/glUploadImageResource.mjs:5-10).
confirmed.failure_scenario: new ImageSource({resource: videoEl}) with no width attribute set, then render: the texture stays transparent or black.
confirmed.game_impact: None today. A grep of src/ finds no video texture usage.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Check resourceWidth (naturalWidth/videoWidth/displayWidth/width) instead of .width.

primary.reasoning:
The code confirms it. In src/engine2d/gpu/GpuTextures.ts:144, upload() returns early when `(img).width === 0` for every non-typed-array resource. On an HTMLVideoElement, `.width` is the HTML width attribute, which is 0 unless the page sets it. It is not the intrinsic size. TextureSource.resourceWidth (TextureSource.ts:173-175) reads `naturalWidth || videoWidth || displayWidth || width`, so the source and the GPU texture get the correct pixelWidth, but the texture is never filled. HTMLVideoElement is a declared resource type (TextureSource.ts:24, ImageSource generic at :244, RhiImageSource in src/rendering/rhi/types.ts:87). TextureSource.from() also sends any video to ImageSource, because ImageSource is its fallback.

Pixi reference: master ran WebGL, where glUploadImageResource (node_modules/pixi.js/lib/rendering/renderers/gl/texture/uploaders/glUploadImageResource.mjs:4-28) uploads unconditionally using source.resourceWidth/resourceHeight. Pixi's WebGPU uploader (gpu/texture/uploaders/gpuUploadImageSource.mjs:8-26) returns early only when the resource is null, then copies `min(gpuTexture.width, resourceWidth || pixelWidth)`. Neither has a width===0 guard.

Repro: tmp/review/verify-renderer-resources-5/video.test.ts uses NullRhiDevice and WebGPURenderer to render a Sprite over new ImageSource({resource}).
- Control, an image-like object {width:16, naturalWidth:16}: rhi.uploadImage is called once.
- Video-like object {width:0, height:0, videoWidth:16, videoHeight:16}: source.pixelWidth is 16, the texture is created, and rhi.uploadImage is called 0 times.

Both tests passed, which demonstrates the bug: the texture stays uninitialized (transparent or black), where Pixi would have uploaded the frame.

Game impact: none. Searching src/ outside engine2d for HTMLVideoElement, createElement('video'), VideoSource, .mp4 or .webm finds no game code that uses video. The only 'video' hits are a comment in SpriteEntity.ts that mentions the offline tools/video_to_atlas pipeline, and an Assets test note that engine2d does not load videos. The game loads animation as atlases, so it never takes this path. Severity is low.
primary.fix_suggestion: In GpuTextures.upload (src/engine2d/gpu/GpuTextures.ts:144), change the guard to use the intrinsic size: `if (!source.resourceWidth || !source.resourceHeight) return;` in place of `if (img.width === 0) return;`. This still skips unloaded images (naturalWidth is 0) and videos with no frame yet (videoWidth is 0, readyState < HAVE_CURRENT_DATA), and it lets loaded videos upload, matching Pixi's resourceWidth-based uploaders. As an option, also clamp the copy extent to min(texture size, resourceWidth/resourceHeight) the way Pixi's gpuUploadImageSource does.

confirmed.title: Mipmaps are never created or generated, so autoGenerateMipmaps / mipLevelCount have no effect (HUD flame sprite sheet)
confirmed.description: GpuTextures.get() creates every RHI texture without a mipLevels field (lines 68-73), and upload() at line 131 never builds a mip chain. TextureSource.updateMipmaps() (TextureSource.ts:213) emits 'updateMipmaps', but nothing listens for it. As a result, source.autoGenerateMipmaps = true and mipLevelCount are silently ignored, and the texture always has a single level. Master's Pixi WebGL does three things at first upload: it computes mipLevelCount = floor(log2(maxDim))+1, calls gl.generateMipmap, and uses a trilinear LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR min filter because mipLevelCount > 1 and mipmapFilter is 'linear'. The RHI already accepts mipLevels (LumaRhiDevice.ts:1011, RenderGraph mipLevels) and luma ships generate-mipmaps-webgpu, so a fix is feasible.
confirmed.reference: node_modules/pixi.js/lib/rendering/renderers/gl/texture/GlTextureSystem.mjs:147-149 (mipLevelCount from autoGenerateMipmaps), :174 (mip filter when mipLevelCount>1), :217-224 (gl.generateMipmap after upload); WebGPU equivalent gpu/texture/GpuTextureSystem.mjs _initSource/onSourceUpdate -> onUpdateMipmaps
confirmed.failure_scenario: Repro tmp/review/shader-uniforms-textures/mip.test.ts: a BufferImageSource with autoGenerateMipmaps=true, scaleMode='linear', drawn as a Sprite at scale 0.25 is created with mipLevels undefined (1 level), and no mip generation is recorded. In the game the 588x612 flame sheet (49x102 frames, 4x resolution) is drawn at scale about 0.26 (HUD.ts:1219-1221, FLAME_SHEET_SCALE_PER_H). Master samples with trilinear mips. The branch samples level 0 with plain bilinear at about 4:1 minification, so the thin strokes alias and shimmer every animation frame. That flicker is exactly what the code comment at HUD.ts:1160 ('开 mipmap + 线性采样，不然细刻线一动就闪') says it guards against.
confirmed.game_impact: src/ui/HUD.ts:1161-1163 (loadFlameSheet: tex.source.autoGenerateMipmaps = true; scaleMode='linear'; update()). These three always-visible HUD flame sprites are animated at 24 fps and scaled to about 1/4 in normal play. The same line exists on master (.tools/game_parity_ref/.../src/ui/HUD.ts:1161). No other game call site sets autoGenerateMipmaps.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In GpuTextures.get(): when source.autoGenerateMipmaps is set, set mipLevelCount = floor(log2(max(pixelWidth,pixelHeight)))+1, as Pixi does. Pass mipLevels to createTexture. After each upload, generate the chain (luma generateMipmapsWebGPU or a blit pass). Also listen for 'updateMipmaps' so render-texture sources can regenerate.

primary.reasoning:
I reproduced this with a side-by-side vitest. Both tests pass: `npx vitest run tmp/review/verify-shader-uniforms-textures-0/mip.test.ts`. Each test takes a 588x612 rgba8 BufferImageSource shaped like the HUD flame sheet, sets autoGenerateMipmaps=true and scaleMode='linear', then calls update() before first use, which is the same order as HUD.ts:1161-1163.

Pixi side: real pixi.js GlTextureSystem, driven through a recording gl proxy with a WebGL2 context stub. When the texture is first bound:
- source.mipLevelCount becomes 10 (floor(log2(612))+1), set at GlTextureSystem.mjs:147-149.
- texParameteri(TEXTURE_2D, TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR) is issued. updateStyle passes mipmaps=mipLevelCount>1 (:174) into applyStyleParams, which maps linear/linear to the trilinear filter.
- TEXTURE_MAX_LEVEL is set to 9 by _applyMipRange.
- gl.generateMipmap is called after the upload (:217-224).

engine2d side: WebGPURenderer on NullRhiDevice. The same source is drawn as a Sprite at scale 0.25:
- createTexture is called for 'flame-sheet' without mipLevels (1 level). The desc is built at GpuTextures.ts:68-74 and has no mip field.
- source.mipLevelCount stays 1, because nothing computes it.
- The source has 0 'updateMipmaps' listeners. TextureSource.ts:213-214 emits to nobody.
- The RHI log has no mip generation.

upload() (GpuTextures.ts:131-146) writes only level 0. The sampler does receive mipmapFilter 'linear' (GpuTextures.ts:108), but with a single level this is plain bilinear. Result: master samples a trilinear mip chain, and the branch samples level 0 bilinear at about 4:1 minification (about 2:1 at DPR 2).

The RHI already has what a fix needs:
- LumaRhiDevice.createTexture forwards mipLevels (LumaRhiDevice.ts:1026).
- Luma exposes device.generateMipmapsWebGPU(texture) (node_modules/@luma.gl/webgpu/dist/adapter/webgpu-device.d.ts:68).

confirmed.title: GPU buffers of geometries destroyed without destroyBuffers (or never destroyed) leak forever; master frees them through Pixi GC and Geometry.destroy
confirmed.description: GpuBuffers keeps a strong Map<Buffer, Entry> and releases an entry only when the engine2d Buffer emits 'destroy' (line 51). engine2d has no GC for idle resources: nothing uses autoGarbageCollect or _gcLastUsed for buffers or textures. Geometry.destroy(false) (shader/Geometry.ts:164-172) does not destroy any buffer, not even the index buffer. Master behaves differently in two ways. (a) Pixi Geometry.destroy() always calls this.indexBuffer?.destroy(). (b) Every other Buffer has autoGarbageCollect = true and sits in GlBufferSystem's GCManagedHash, so GCSystem (gcActive defaults to true, gcMaxUnusedTime 60 s) unloads its GL buffer once it is unused and drops the reference. On the branch, every Buffer of a geometry the game abandons keeps its RHI buffer, its CPU typed array and its Geometry, through the buffer's listener context, until the renderer is destroyed.

Afterwards 15 RHI buffers (aPosition, aUV and index for each of the 5 meshes) are still alive and still referenced by GpuBuffers.entries. In master the index buffer is destroyed immediately and the other two are GC'd within about 60-90 s.

(1) Game.clearEntityShadows / destroyEntityShadowEntry (Game.ts:7090, 7648) call PlanarEntityShadow.destroy(), which calls castGeometry.destroy() and contactGeometry.destroy() without destroyBuffers (EntityShadow.ts:1288,1291). That leaks 6 buffers per shadowed NPC, hotspot or player on every scene change. (2) LitSpriteQuad.destroy() (CharacterLitSprite.ts:1257-1260) only destroys the mesh; its comment wrongly says 'includes geometry'. It runs from SpriteEntity.refreshBakedShading/disableBakedShading (SpriteEntity.ts:531,549,1323) on every scene lighting refresh and leaks 4 buffers (aPosition, aUV, aLocal, index) per lit character each time. (3) BurnRenderer.ts:448, overlayBlendShader.ts:175 and breathingOverlayMesh.ts:159 also call geometry.destroy() without destroyBuffers. Each buffer holds 24-64 bytes of data plus a WebGPU allocation and JS objects, so the growth is unbounded but slow. There is no visible rendering difference.

Have GpuBuffers (and ideally GpuTextures for autoGarbageCollect sources) track a last-used frame or time and release entries idle for more than 60 s, or release a geometry's buffers when the Geometry emits 'destroy' and nothing else references them. A narrower alternative is to fix the game call sites to pass destroy(true), but that diverges from the ownership contract master relied on.

primary.reasoning:
The finding holds. I reproduced it with `npx vitest run tmp/review/verify-shader-uniforms-textures-1/geomleak.test.ts --silent=false`, and all 3 cases pass.

(A) Same `MeshGeometry.destroy()` call, side by side:
- Pixi: `indexBuffer.destroyed === true`.
- engine2d: the index buffer never emits 'destroy'.
- Cause: engine2d `src/engine2d/shader/Geometry.ts:164-172` only destroys buffers when `destroyBuffers` is true. Pixi `node_modules/pixi.js/lib/rendering/renderers/shared/geometry/Geometry.mjs:137-149` always runs `this.unload(); this.indexBuffer?.destroy()`.

(B) The master mechanism, driven with Pixi's real `GCSystem` and `GCManagedHash` classes, a fake renderer and a mocked `performance.now`:
- A Pixi Buffer added to the hash has its gpuData destroyed and is removed from the hash after 61 s idle.
- The defaults are `gcActive: true`, `gcMaxUnusedTime: 60000` and `gcFrequency: 30000` (`GCSystem.mjs:298-302`).
- `Buffer.autoGarbageCollect = true` (`Buffer.mjs:34`), and `GlBufferSystem.createGLBuffer` calls `_managedBuffers.add` (`GlBufferSystem.mjs:173-184`).
- Master never overrides the gc options. I grepped the master checkout's `src` for gcActive, gcMaxUnusedTime and autoGarbageCollect and found no hits.
- Nuance: in the GC path the hash slot is nulled before `unload()`, so `onBufferUnload` (`gl.deleteBuffer`) is skipped. The WebGLBuffer is still released, because the JS handle is dropped and the browser collects it. Master memory is bounded either way.

(C) The branch on NullRhiDevice, which works in node:
- Setup: 5 teardowns, each using the EntityShadow pattern (`mesh.destroy(); shader.destroy(); geometry.destroy()`) plus the LitSpriteQuad pattern (`mesh.destroy()` only). Then 100 more frames of an empty scene.
- Result: 30 RHI buffers still alive (`attribute-mesh-positions`, `attribute-mesh-uvs`, `index-mesh-buffer` × 10), and `GpuBuffers.entries.size === 30`.
- Cause: engine2d has no idle GC. `GpuBuffers.ts:51` releases an entry only on Buffer 'destroy'. The Map lives on the renderer-wide scope (`WebGPURenderer.ts:148-151`) until `renderer.destroy()`.

Game hits the path:
1. `Game.clearEntityShadows` (`src/core/Game.ts:7645`) runs on every scene unload (`Game.ts:6514`) and every shadow rebuild (`Game.ts:7029`). `destroyEntityShadowEntry` (`Game.ts:7072/7078/7086`) also reaches it. Each goes through `PlanarEntityShadow.destroy` (`src/rendering/EntityShadow.ts:1288,1291`), which destroys the geometry without `destroyBuffers`. That leaves 6 buffers per shadow, where master drops the index buffers at once and the rest after 60 s.
2. `LitSpriteQuad.destroy` (`src/rendering/CharacterLitSprite.ts:1257-1260`) only destroys the mesh. The engine2d and Pixi `Mesh.destroy` also leave the geometry alone. It is called from `SpriteEntity.refreshBakedShading` / `disableBakedShading` / `disposeAttachmentLit` (`src/rendering/SpriteEntity.ts:531,549,1323`), which Game drives at `Game.ts:6980-6981,8082,8181`. That leaves 4 buffers per lit character or attachment per refresh. Master has identical code at `CharacterLitSprite.ts:768` and relied on Pixi GC for all 4.
3. Other call sites: `BurnRenderer.ts:448`, `overlayBlendShader.ts:175`, `breathingOverlayMesh.ts:159`.

Severity: medium. The growth is unbounded and per scene, but each step is tiny: a few 32-64 byte GPU buffers plus the JS Buffer, typed array and Geometry. The Buffer keeps the Geometry through its listener. Nothing renders differently and nothing crashes in any realistic session length. It fits "small leak" better than critical.
primary.fix_suggestion:
Mirror Pixi 8.17:
1. In `src/engine2d/shader/Geometry.ts` `destroy()`, always destroy the index buffer, as Pixi does. After the `destroyBuffers` loop, add `this.indexBuffer?.destroy();`. This is before the fields are cleared. A shared index buffer is destroyed the same way in Pixi, so the behaviour matches.
2. Add Pixi-style idle collection to `src/engine2d/gpu/GpuBuffers.ts`:
   - Give engine2d `Buffer` an `autoGarbageCollect = true` field.
   - In `get()`, stamp `e.lastUsed = now`, where `now` is `performance.now()` captured once per `render()`.
   - Register the listener as `buffer.once('destroy', this.release, this)` rather than a closure, so it can be removed.
   - Add a `gc(now)` pass that the renderer calls at most every 30 s (gcFrequency) after a frame. It releases each entry with `now - lastUsed > 60000` whose `buffer.autoGarbageCollect` is true: `e.buffer.destroy(); this.entries.delete(buffer); buffer.off('destroy', this.release, this)`.
   - A later `get()` recreates the RHI buffer with `updateId = -1`, so it re-uploads. This is the same re-upload-on-reuse semantics as Pixi's GC.
   - Because `get()` runs during planning of the current frame, anything used this frame has a fresh stamp and cannot be collected while in flight.
   - Optionally apply the same idle GC to `GpuTextures` for sources with `autoGarbageCollect`.
3. Do not change the game call sites. Master's ownership contract, where the caller calls `geometry.destroy()` and the renderer GC reclaims the vertex buffers, should keep working unchanged.

confirmed.title: Geometry attribute format defaults to float32x2 instead of being inferred from the WGSL @location type; stride sums only the attributes the shader uses
confirmed.description: addAttribute() fills in format 'float32x2' when none is given. Pixi leaves it undefined and ensureAttributes() later fills it from the shader's attribute type (f32 -> float32, vec4<f32> -> float32x4, and so on). The stride is also computed differently. Pipelines.layout (Pipelines.ts:153-155) sums the formats of the attributes the shader declares only. Pixi's ensureStartAndStride sums every geometry attribute on that buffer, whether or not the shader uses it.

primary.reasoning:
Both parts of the finding reproduce. The repro runs engine2d on NullRhiDevice, with a spy on createRenderPipeline, next to Pixi 8.17 (Geometry + GpuProgram.from + ensureAttributes from the gl ensureAttributes.mjs module, the same one PipelineSystem.mjs:67 calls). Output is in tmp/review/verify-shader-uniforms-textures-2/out.txt.

1) Format default. The shader declares `@location(1) aColor: vec4<f32>` and the geometry is built as `{aPosition: Float32Array, aColor: Float32Array}` with no formats.
- engine2d records stream1 = {stride 8, aColor format float32x2}.
- Pixi gets aColor = {format float32x4, stride 16}.
- Cause: src/engine2d/shader/Geometry.ts:90 does `const format = opt.format ?? 'float32x2'`, so the format is fixed when the attribute is added. The reported line 99 is slightly off; the code is at line 90.
- Pixi instead does `attribute.format ??= attributeData.format` (pixi.js/lib/rendering/renderers/gl/shader/program/ensureAttributes.mjs:10), taking the type from WGSL_TO_VERTEX_TYPES (gpu/shader/utils/extractAttributesFromGpuProgram.mjs:4-35).
- Result: wrong stride, and only 2 components are fetched.

2) Stride over a subset. One interleaved buffer holds aPosition@0, aUnused@8 and aColor@16, all float32x2 with no stride given, and the shader uses only aPosition and aColor.
- engine2d computes stride 16 (Pipelines.ts:143-154 skips attributes the shader does not declare, then sums the rest).
- Pixi computes stride 24 (ensureAttributes.mjs:28-34 sums every attribute on the buffer).
- With stride 16, every vertex after the first reads the wrong data.

Game impact: none.
- Every game Geometry passes an explicit format and gives each attribute its own buffer: backgroundSway.ts:1041-1046, VfxBoltBatchMesh.ts:45-52, VfxPlateBatchMesh.ts:96-104, VfxBeamView.ts:175-177, VfxBatchMesh.ts:71-79, CharacterLitSprite.ts:1211-1214.
- MeshGeometry sets 'float32x2' explicitly (src/engine2d/mesh/MeshGeometry.ts:28,34).
- Engine2d's own quadGeometry (FrameBuilder.ts:131-134) is explicit, with stride 8.
- No game code creates an interleaved buffer where the shader skips an attribute.

Severity is therefore low: this is a Pixi API path the game does not use.
primary.fix_suggestion: (a) In Geometry.addAttribute (Geometry.ts:90), keep `format: opt.format` and let it stay undefined. Adjust getSize() and the bounds code to cope with a missing format. (b) In Pipelines.layout, resolve each attribute's format as `attr.format ?? WGSL_TO_VERTEX_TYPES[program.attributes.find(a=>a.name===name).type] ?? 'float32'`, as Pixi's ensureAttributes does. Write it back to the attribute with `??=` so geometryVersion and getSize see it. (c) Compute the implicit stride per buffer over ALL geometry attributes that share that buffer, not only the ones the shader uses (Pixi's ensureStartAndStride). Keep building the RHI attribute list from the shader-declared subset only, because luma rejects attributes the shader does not use. For an attribute the shader lacks and whose format is undefined, Pixi only warns, so fall back to 'float32x2' for the stride sum or skip it with a warning.

primary.fix_suggestion:
Port Pixi's idle-texture GC into engine2d. This is minimal and matches master:

1. **Track last use.** In GpuTextures, give Entry a `lastUsed: number` and set it to `performance.now()` on every `get()`, including cache hits.

2. **Register listeners once.** Record the sources that already have listeners (a WeakSet, or a flag on the Entry). Otherwise a GC'd source that comes back registers duplicate 'unload' listeners. In `release()`, also detach them with `source.off('unload', ...)` and `source.off('destroy', ...)`, using stored bound handlers.

3. **Collect idle textures.** Add a `collect(now, maxUnused = 60000)` method. For each entry with `source.autoGarbageCollect && now - e.lastUsed >= maxUnused`, call `source.unload()`. That emits 'unload', which runs `release()`: `onRelease`, `texture.destroy()`, map delete. Since unload bumps `_resourceId`, the texture is simply re-uploaded on next use. Call `collect` from WebGPURenderer after `render()`, throttled to every 30 s (Pixi `gcFrequency`). Put the options behind `gcActive` (default true), `gcMaxUnusedTime` (60000) and `gcFrequency` (30000), matching GCSystem.defaultOptions.

4. **Make gradients eligible.** In src/engine2d/graphics/fill/FillGradient.ts:180 and :238, construct the CanvasSource with `autoGarbageCollect: true`, matching Pixi's ImageSource there.

5. **Leave other sources alone.** Do not collect sources with `autoGarbageCollect` false: RenderTexture, pool textures (TexturePool.ts:42), and default CanvasSource / Text textures. That matches Pixi, where only autoGC sources are unloaded.

6. **Regression test.** Adapt the repro: after simulating more than 60 s idle, `entries.size` returns to its baseline and the RHI textures of the dropped gradients are destroyed. A gradient that is rendered every frame must never be collected.

I tried to refute the claim and could not. It holds.

- FillGradient.ts:180 (linear) and :238 (radial) build the texture on a CanvasSource. The only way it gets destroyed is FillGradient.destroy() (:252-253).
- GraphicsContext.clear() (GraphicsContext.ts:506-512) only drops instructions.
- GraphicsContext.destroy() only destroys `_fillStyle`/`_strokeStyle` textures, and only when `options.texture` is set (:607-624). It never touches textures in `instructions`.
- Graphics.destroy({children:true}) does not destroy the owned context (Graphics.ts:147-152). This matches Pixi.

**Pixi / master**
- FillGradient.mjs:95/161 uses ImageSource, and ImageSource.mjs:9 sets `autoGarbageCollect = true`.
- GlTextureSystem.mjs:30-35 puts every uploaded source in a GCManagedHash. It touches `_gcLastUsed` on bind (:93, :363).
- GCSystem.mjs:298-305 defaults to gcActive true, gcMaxUnusedTime 60000 ms, gcFrequency 30000 ms. `runOnHash` (:249-266) calls `source.unload()`, which deletes the GL texture and nulls the hash slot (GCManagedHash.mjs:24-32).
- Master's Renderer.ts:138-143 passes no gc options, so these defaults apply. Master creates gradients at the same call sites as the branch (UIDecor.ts:28/360, PanelSkin.ts:236, MenuUI.ts:1919, ObjectExamineScene.ts:1822).
- Master therefore reclaims GPU memory for dropped gradients 60-90 s after last use. The branch never does.

**Repro (my own, NullRhiDevice + WebGPURenderer)**
- The test uses the UIButton hover pattern: `bg.clear()` then a new linear FillGradient fill, then render, 30 times. It then renders 200 idle frames with nothing drawn.
- `GpuTextures.entries` went from 0 to 32 and stayed at 32. That is one entry per gradient plus renderer-internal ones, and nothing is evicted.
- The reviewer's radial/destroy({children:true}) repro shows the same.

**Game hits the path**
- PanelSkin.createPanel (src/ui/PanelSkin.ts:233-247) makes a radial 256x256 vignette for every skin with wood>=WOOD_PANEL or an explicit vignette. createPanel has 46 call sites, including DialogueUI.layoutFrame (DialogueUI.ts:628, which runs on dialogue open and resize) and UIWindow chrome.
- UIDecor.drawSelectedRow (UIDecor.ts:360) makes a linear gradient per call. UIButton.redraw calls it on pointerover and pointerout (UIButton.ts:111-112, 153) for ghost buttons.

**Severity: high, not critical**
- Growth is per UI interaction (panel open, hover), not per frame. I checked the callers and none are per-frame; WaterPullPanel.ts:222 even avoids that deliberately.
- It is roughly 256 KB of GPU memory plus a 256 KB canvas per vignette panel build, and roughly 1 KB plus a canvas element per ghost-button hover.
- It is unbounded and diverges from master, but it will not break frames in a normal-length session.

**Related, same root cause**
- The branch's ImageSource sets autoGarbageCollect=true but it is never honoured. Asset textures that go unused for 60 s stay resident on the GPU, where master would evict them and re-upload on demand. Memory-only divergence, no visual difference.
- Minor: GpuTextures.get adds a new `once('destroy')` and `on('unload')` listener every time an entry is re-created, for example after an unload or a resourceId change. The 'unload' listeners accumulate on long-lived sources.
second.fix_suggestion:
Port Pixi 8.17's texture GC into GpuTextures, keeping Pixi's defaults and semantics:
1. Add a per-renderer `now` (performance.now()) and set it in WebGPURenderer.render's prerender step.
2. In GpuTextures.get, stamp `entry.lastUsed = now` on every call. This covers every bind site: FrameBuilder.ts:358, :461, :500, :510, :582, :584 and :741.
3. Every gcFrequency (30000 ms), after a render, walk `entries`. For each one where `now - lastUsed >= gcMaxUnusedTime` (60000 ms) and `source.autoGarbageCollect` is true, call `source.unload()`. That emits 'unload', which reaches `release()`, which destroys the RHI texture, calls onRelease and deletes the entry. Skip render-target sources and pool sources (autoGarbageCollect is false for those, as in Pixi).
4. Register the 'destroy'/'unload' listeners once per source (for example behind a WeakSet or a flag on the entry) and remove them in `release()`, so the Map and its closures stop pinning the source and repeated re-uploads do not stack listeners.
5. Make FillGradient's texture GC-eligible as in Pixi: build it on ImageSource (FillGradient.mjs:95/161 does this), or pass `autoGarbageCollect: true` to the CanvasSource at FillGradient.ts:180 and :238.
6. Expose gcActive / gcMaxUnusedTime / gcFrequency with Pixi's defaults (true, 60000, 30000).
7. Add a regression test: NullRhiDevice, a fake clock, a dropped gradient graphic; advance past 90 s and assert `entries` shrinks, and that the next use re-uploads.

confirmed.title: Sprite.roundPixels changes take effect after the first render, while master's SpritePipe fixes the value at the sprite's first render
confirmed.description: engine2d Sprite.collectRenderables copies `this._roundPixels` into the batch element on every frame (Sprite.ts:141). Text.ts:112, HTMLText.ts:113, NineSliceSprite and batched Mesh do the same. Pixi 8.17 sets BatchableSprite.roundPixels only once, in SpritePipe._initGPUSprite, when the sprite is first rendered. _updateBatchableSprite copies only bounds and texture after that, and DefaultBatcher reads element.roundPixels. Changing sprite.roundPixels after the first render therefore does nothing in master for the life of the sprite (its _gpuData is only cleared by unload/destroy). The branch honours every change. A side-by-side check (tmp/review/text-sprite-mesh/roundpixels.test.ts) gives Pixi SpritePipe [0,0] and engine2d [0,1] for render, set roundPixels=true, render.
confirmed.reference: node_modules/pixi.js/lib/scene/sprite/SpritePipe.mjs:25-28 (_updateBatchableSprite copies bounds/texture only) and :33-41 (_initGPUSprite: `batchableSprite.roundPixels = this._renderer._roundPixels | sprite._roundPixels`, set once); node_modules/pixi.js/lib/rendering/batcher/shared/DefaultBatcher.mjs:27,75 (uses element.roundPixels). Same init-only pattern in CanvasTextPipe.mjs:64, HTMLTextPipe.mjs:87, NineSliceSpritePipe.mjs:51, MeshPipe.mjs:115 (batched).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Scene load: SceneManager.instantiateHotspot adds hotspot.container, with its displaySprite created by setDisplayTexture, to the entityLayer (src/systems/SceneManager.ts:1479-1484). The load then awaits more NPC texture loads and the depth and lighting loaders (SceneManager.ts:1876-1930), and the Application ticker keeps rendering during those awaits (nothing pauses it and the world is not hidden). The on-screen display sprites are therefore rendered with roundPixels=false. Only after loading finishes does Game call syncEntityPixelDensityMatch (src/core/Game.ts:8014). With game_config entityPixelDensityMatch:true and a sprite background (so dBg is non-null), this sets `displaySprite.roundPixels = true` (src/entities/Hotspot.ts:344). Master keeps drawing those sprites unrounded, because the value was fixed at their first render. The branch starts rounding their vertices to device pixels, a shift of up to 0.5 device px that moves in whole-pixel steps while the camera pans. NPC and player inner sprites go through SpriteEntity.setPixelDensityMatchActive (src/rendering/SpriteEntity.ts:1626) and are affected the same way when they are drawn by the plain sprite path, i.e. when no lit quad has replaced them. The dev-mode override cycle (Game.ts:3787-3790) also toggles snapping live on the branch but not in master.
confirmed.game_impact: Hotspot display images (and NPC/player sprites whenever they are drawn by the plain sprite path) that are on screen during scene load are pixel-snapped on the branch but not in master. This shows up as sub-pixel position differences and different motion (snapping versus smooth sampling) during camera pans, and tools/ab_compare pixel diffs on hotspot sprites will flag it. Master's result depends on timing (whether a frame rendered before the sync), so the difference appears per scene and per hotspot.
confirmed.suggested_fix: If exact master parity is wanted, match Pixi. Keep the roundPixels value on the Sprite's batch element as it was at the first collect, e.g. set `_batchable.roundPixels` once when the element is first used (and again after unload/destroy re-creates GPU data), instead of re-reading _roundPixels every frame. Apply the same to Text/HTMLText/NineSliceSprite/batched Mesh. Alternatively treat master's behaviour as a Pixi bug and accept the difference explicitly, since the game code clearly intends the toggle to take effect.

primary.reasoning:
**Reproduced.** The repro runs both engines on the same sequence: render a sprite, set `roundPixels = true`, render again twice. It reads the round bit (low 16 bits of the `textureIdAndRound` word) from the actual packed vertex data.
- Pixi 8.17 side: the real `SpritePipe` (`addRenderable`, then `updateRenderable`) feeding the real `DefaultBatcher.prototype.packQuadAttributes`. Round bits are `[0, 0, 0]`.
- engine2d side: a full `WebGPURenderer.render` on `NullRhiDevice`, with the bit read from the vertex buffer passed to `writeBuffer`. Round bits are `[0, 1, 1]`.

**Code evidence.**
- Pixi sets the value once and never updates it:
  - `node_modules/pixi.js/lib/scene/sprite/SpritePipe.mjs:39` sets `roundPixels` once, in `_initGPUSprite`.
  - `SpritePipe.mjs:25-28` (`_updateBatchableSprite`) copies only `bounds` and `texture`.
  - `node_modules/pixi.js/lib/scene/view/ViewContainer.mjs:57-58` (the setter) only stores `_roundPixels` and triggers no re-init.
  - `_gpuData` is cleared only by `unload()` (`ViewContainer.mjs:92-98`) or destroy. `RenderableGCSystem` (active by default, 60s unused) can also unload it, so an off-screen object that is later redrawn picks up the new value. That is a minor nuance.
- Both packers read `element.roundPixels`: Pixi at `DefaultBatcher.mjs:27` and `:75`, engine2d at `src/engine2d/gpu/Batcher.ts:140` and `:170`.
- engine2d re-copies the value on every collect: `src/engine2d/sprite/Sprite.ts:141`. `Text.ts:112`, `HTMLText.ts:113`, `NineSliceSprite.ts:276` and `Mesh.ts:145` do the same.

**Game path.**
- Master and branch toggle `roundPixels` at run time in the same places:
  - `Hotspot.applyEntityPixelDensityMatch`: master `src/entities/Hotspot.ts:332/340`, branch `:336/344`.
  - `SpriteEntity.setPixelDensityMatchActive`: `src/rendering/SpriteEntity.ts:1626`.
- The toggle is driven by `Game.syncEntityPixelDensityMatch` (master `Game.ts:9269`). It is called from the `scene:ready` handler (master `Game.ts:8072`), the runtime-NPC `onSpawned` hook, and the debug toggles.
- `public/assets/data/game_config.json:19` sets `entityPixelDensityMatch: true`.
- Hotspot display sprites are always drawn by the plain sprite path (`Hotspot.ts` has no lit quad).
- In master's `SceneManager.loadScene`, the hotspots are added (`:1860/1870`) before later awaits: NPC instantiation, then `depthLoader` (`:1916`) and `lightingLoader` (`:1925`), which call `sceneDepthSystem.load` and `sceneLighting.load`. `scene:ready` is emitted only after those awaits.
- Nothing hides the world or stops the ticker during load; the transition mask only covers the world and does not stop Pixi collecting it. So any hotspot display sprite that renders during an await spanning a frame keeps `roundPixels = 0` in master for its lifetime, while the branch switches to 1 at `scene:ready`.
- The player's inner `Sprite` lasts across scenes, so in master its value is fixed at its very first render (before any sync). Whenever it is drawn plainly (no `litQuad`; see `SpriteEntity.ts:576`), the branch rounds it and master does not.
- The dev override toggles also take effect live on the branch but not in master.
- Caveat: whether a frame actually lands inside those awaits in master depends on I/O timing. I did not measure it in a browser; this is inferred from the code structure.

**Severity: medium.** The effect is a shift of at most 0.5 device px, snapping versus smooth sub-pixel motion during camera pans. Nothing crashes or breaks. It also has a filter interaction: the hotspot's depth and blur filters sample an input that is rounded in one version and not in the other. Master's behaviour is arguably a Pixi quirk that the game code did not intend, but the task goal is zero divergence, so it counts as a real divergence. `tools/ab_compare` should flag it on hotspots that are visible during load.
primary.fix_suggestion:
Copy `roundPixels` into the batch element only on the first collect after the element is (re)created, as Pixi's `_initGPUSprite` does. Do not re-copy it every frame.

In `src/engine2d/sprite/Sprite.ts`:
1. Add a field `private _batchInit = false`.
2. In `collectRenderables`, replace `b.roundPixels = this._roundPixels;` with:
   `if (!this._batchInit) { b.roundPixels = /* renderer._roundPixels | */ this._roundPixels; this._batchInit = true; }`
   OR in the renderer-level flag if engine2d applies it elsewhere, to mirror `this._renderer._roundPixels | sprite._roundPixels`.
3. Reset `_batchInit = false` wherever Pixi would drop `_gpuData`: `unload()` and `destroy()`, and the renderable-GC equivalent if engine2d has one.

Apply the same one-time init to:
- `Text.ts:112`, matching `CanvasTextPipe.mjs:64`.
- `HTMLText.ts:113`, matching `HTMLTextPipe.mjs:87`.
- `NineSliceSprite.ts:276`, matching `NineSliceSpritePipe.mjs:51`.
- `Mesh.ts:145` for batched meshes only, matching `MeshPipe.mjs:115`. The non-batched mesh uniform path (`MeshPipe.mjs:83`, `FrameBuilder.ts:490`) re-reads `roundPixels` every frame in Pixi too, so leave it as is.

Add a regression test like the repro: render, toggle, render, then assert the round bit is still 0.

confirmed.title: Sprite/NineSlice constructors: `anchor: 0` or `anchor: null` behave differently from Pixi
confirmed.description: The engine2d Sprite constructor tests `if (anchor !== undefined) this.anchor = anchor; else if (texture.defaultAnchor) ...`. Pixi tests truthiness: `if (anchor) ... else if (texture.defaultAnchor)`. For `anchor: 0`, Pixi falls through to texture.defaultAnchor while engine2d sets 0 and ignores defaultAnchor. For `anchor: null`, engine2d calls `_anchor.copyFrom(null)` and throws, while Pixi ignores it. NineSliceSprite matches Pixi (`if (anchor)`).
confirmed.reference: node_modules/pixi.js/lib/scene/sprite/Sprite.mjs constructor: `if (anchor) { this.anchor = anchor; } else if (texture.defaultAnchor) { this.anchor = texture.defaultAnchor; }`
confirmed.failure_scenario: new Sprite({ texture: spritesheetFrameWithDefaultAnchor, anchor: 0 }): Pixi uses the frame's defaultAnchor and engine2d uses (0,0). new Sprite({ texture, anchor: null }): engine2d throws a TypeError in ObservablePoint.copyFrom.
confirmed.game_impact: Not hit by the game: it loads no spritesheets, so no texture has a defaultAnchor, and a grep finds no `anchor: null` or `anchor: 0` in Sprite options under src/.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use `if (anchor)` to match Pixi.

I reproduced this with a side-by-side vitest at tmp/review/verify-text-sprite-mesh-2/anchor.test.ts, and both tests pass, so the divergence is real.
(1) Anchor 0 on a texture with a default anchor. The texture was created with defaultAnchor {x:0.5, y:1} and the sprite with anchor: 0. Pixi's Sprite ends up with anchor (0.5, 1): `if (anchor)` treats 0 as false and falls through to the texture's default anchor (node_modules/pixi.js/lib/scene/sprite/Sprite.mjs:33-36). engine2d's Sprite ends up with (0, 0), because src/engine2d/sprite/Sprite.ts:38 checks `if (anchor !== undefined)`.
(2) Anchor null. Pixi's `new Sprite({texture, anchor: null})` does not throw. engine2d throws a TypeError: the anchor setter (Sprite.ts:82-84) passes null to ObservablePoint.copyFrom, which reads p.x (ObservablePoint.ts:32).
The other constructors that take an anchor already match Pixi: NineSliceSprite.ts:120 and AbstractText.ts:62 both use `if (anchor)`.
The game never reaches this code. Every `new Sprite(...)` under src/ outside engine2d passes a Texture or no argument, never an options object (examples: UIDecor.ts:387, MapUI.ts:350, SpriteEntity.ts:346/1770, CutsceneRenderer.ts:704/1103, WaterMinigameScene.ts:132). Only the Texture-or-nothing form of the constructor is used, and the anchor comes out as undefined there. The only options-object construction is NineSliceSprite in PanelSkin.ts:188, and that path already matches Pixi. No game code sets defaultAnchor either. Severity stays low: the difference only shows up through API use the game does not make.
primary.fix_suggestion: In src/engine2d/sprite/Sprite.ts:38, change `if (anchor !== undefined) this.anchor = anchor;` to `if (anchor) this.anchor = anchor;` and leave the `else if (texture.defaultAnchor)` branch as it is. This matches the constructor in Pixi 8.17's Sprite.mjs:33-36.

confirmed.title: Culler leaves `culled` stale on inactive nodes, where master (visible=false) recomputed it to false
confirmed.description: `_cullRecursive` returns early when `!container._activeSelf`. That guard does not exist in Pixi's Culler. On master, NPCs and hotspots were hidden with `visible=false`. For such a node Pixi still ran the cull test: `getGlobalBounds` returned an invalid box, which gets normalised to (0,0,0,0). Against the game's padded view (x<0, y<0) that always gives `culled = false`, and Pixi also kept walking into the children. On the branch, presence moved to `setActive(false)`. An absent entity now keeps whatever `culled` value it had before it was deactivated, and its subtree is never visited. This is a semantic change caused by the visible->setActive migration.
confirmed.reference: node_modules/pixi.js/lib/culling/Culler.mjs:14-37 (no visibility or active guard). node_modules/pixi.js/lib/scene/container/bounds/getGlobalBounds.mjs (`if (!target.visible ...) return;` then `if (!bounds.isValid) bounds.set(0,0,0,0)`). Master hid NPCs and hotspots via container.visible.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Repro in tmp/review/events-app-assets/culler.test.ts. The entity layer has an NPC with cullable=true at x=2000 (off screen), culled with view=screen.pad(...), so culled=true. Then hide it: setActive(false) on the branch, visible=false on master. Move it to x=400 and cull again. Branch: culled stays true. Pixi: culled becomes false. Result: {e0:true, e1:true, p0:true, p1:false}.
confirmed.game_impact: Game.updateFrustumCulling (src/core/Game.ts:7188-7208) runs Culler.shared.cull on entityLayer every frame. The shading-drive loops read `child.culled` / `h.container.culled` to skip work (src/core/Game.ts:10741, 10781). For absent entities this gate now depends on a stale value: master always drove them (culled=false), the branch may or may not. The F2 hierarchy panel also shows a stale '已剔除' flag (src/ui/debugHierarchySection.ts:657, debugHierarchyModel.ts:361). Presence is re-derived before culling each tick (InteractionSystem.update at Game.ts:10500, cull at 10675), so I found no path that yields a visible frame difference. confirmed.suggested_fix: When a node is inactive, set `container.culled = false` and return, instead of returning with the old value. Or drop the guard and let getGlobalBounds' inactive check produce the same (0,0,0,0) result Pixi produces for visible=false. Add a regression case to Culler.test.ts.

primary.reasoning:
Reproduced independently. The repro copies Game.updateFrustumCulling: an entity layer whose child is cullable, view = screen.clone().pad(w*m, h*m) so x<0 and y<0, and engine2d's default skipUpdateTransform. It then hides the node, setActive(false) on the branch and visible=false in Pixi, moves it, and culls again. With startX=2000, engine2d gives culled [true, true, true] (off screen, then hidden at x=400, then hidden at x=3000). Pixi gives [true, false, false], and still false with skipUpdateTransform=true. With startX=400 both give false, so the divergence appears only when the node was culled before it was hidden.

Cause: src/engine2d/culling/Culler.ts:49 `if (!container._activeSelf) return;` exits before `culled` is assigned. Pixi's node_modules/pixi.js/lib/culling/Culler.mjs:41-65 has no visible or active guard. Its getGlobalBounds (lib/scene/container/bounds/getGlobalBounds.mjs) returns early for !visible and normalises the invalid bounds to (0,0,0,0). Against the padded view that gives culled=false.

The branch's own getGlobalBounds (src/engine2d/scene/Container.ts:1482-1492) already skips `!_activeSelf` and normalises to (0,0,0,0), so the guard is the only source of the difference. Master hid NPCs with container.visible (master src/entities/Npc.ts:652) and hotspots the same way (master Hotspot.ts:420). The branch uses setActive (src/entities/Npc.ts:660, src/entities/Hotspot.ts:425).

Game impact: Game.updateFrustumCulling (src/core/Game.ts:7188-7208) culls entityLayer every tick at Game.ts:10675. The only readers of `culled` are:
- the shading-drive skips at Game.ts:10741 and 10781;
- the debug hierarchy (src/ui/debugHierarchySection.ts:657, debugHierarchyModel.ts:361).

For an absent entity, master always drove its shading (culled=false). The branch skips it if the stale value is true. That is only wasted or skipped work on an invisible node.

Presence changes reach Npc.applyEffectiveVisible / Hotspot.applyEffectiveActive from InteractionSystem.update (Game.ts:10500), cutscene and dialogue actions in tick, or DOM event handlers between frames. All of these run before the next tick's cull and render, so `culled` is recomputed before anything is drawn.

The only possible visible effect is a one-frame pop-in: an entity is reactivated in a frame where tick returns before the cull, which happens in two places:
- the damage→non-Exploring early return at Game.ts:10497;
- the top-of-tick systemNotePause/Dead returns.
For it to show, the entity must also have been off screen when it was deactivated and be on screen now. That window is very narrow. Severity low: the effect is a stale debug flag, a different per-frame shading work set for absent entities, and at most a theoretical one-frame delay in rare frames.
primary.fix_suggestion: In src/engine2d/culling/Culler.ts, delete line 49 (`if (!container._activeSelf) return;`). Pixi has no such guard. The branch's getGlobalBounds already treats an inactive node as empty bounds, normalised to (0,0,0,0), exactly like Pixi does for visible=false. So without the guard, an inactive node gets the same culled result as master's hidden node (false against the padded view), and Pixi's walk into children is kept. The cullArea branch also then matches Pixi. If the subtree walk is not wanted, the smaller alternative is `if (!container._activeSelf) { container.culled = false; return; }`, which is correct for the game because entity children are never cullable. Add a regression case to Culler.test.ts: cull an off-screen node, setActive(false), move it on screen, cull again, and expect culled === false.

confirmed.title: EventEmitter.off/removeListener with context=null removes nothing (eventemitter3 treats a falsy context as 'any')
confirmed.description: The filter keeps a listener when `context !== undefined && l.ctx !== context`. eventemitter3, which every Pixi Container, Texture and similar object uses, only compares contexts when `context` is truthy. With `null` it removes every listener that matches `fn`. `on(evt, fn)` stores ctx=this, so on the branch `off(evt, fn, null)` never matches and the listener survives. This is also the emitter behind every Container event listener used by EventBoundary._notifyListeners.

confirmed.title: A pipeline that fails compile or validation is still drawn with, and the whole frame's command buffer is lost (black screen) instead of only that draw
confirmed.description: prepareDraw (811-830) and setPipeline (727-745) never check whether the pipeline failed. waitPipelineReady (1432-1450) only detects WGSL compile errors: the device is created with debug:false (line 113), so luma's pushErrorScope and popErrorScope are no-ops (node_modules/@luma.gl/webgpu/dist/adapter/webgpu-device.js:308-323). As a result WebGPURenderPipeline.linkStatus always becomes 'success', even when createRenderPipeline produced an invalid pipeline (validation error or D3D/FXC internal error). Draws with an invalid pipeline, or with a compile-failed shader whose `ready` rejected, still reach GPURenderPassEncoder.setPipeline. Under WebGPU rules that invalidates the whole GPUCommandEncoder, so encoder.finish()/queue.submit discards every pass of the frame. The canvas texture was already acquired, so a cleared (black) frame is presented. The RhiRenderPipeline.ready contract ('失败 reject') is also not met for validation failures.
confirmed.reference: Pixi GL (master): node_modules/pixi.js/lib/rendering/renderers/gl/shader/program/generateProgram.mjs:30-32 only logs a link failure (logProgramError) and continues; draws with the broken program fail individually and the rest of the frame renders.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Any single game shader fails on a user's GPU/driver: a Tint uniformity or deprecation error in a newer Chrome, an FXC 'loop does not terminate' or internal error on a large lighting shader on Windows, or an invalid blend/vertex-format combination. In master only that object or filter disappears. On the branch, every frame that uses the pipeline submits an invalid command buffer and the whole screen stays black for as long as that object or filter is in the scene. The only signal is an uncaptured-error diagnostic.
confirmed.game_impact: Every draw goes through WebGPURenderer.record (src/engine2d/gpu/WebGPURenderer.ts:269-284), which calls setPipeline and draw without checking pipeline status. The large game WGSL shaders (lighting, character shading, vfx, burn) are the likeliest to fail on particular hardware. The same amplification applies to an invalid bind group, e.g. an unfilterable texture bound to a 'float' sampleType.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In createRenderPipeline/createShader, push a native validation+internal error scope on luma.handle regardless of luma debug, and mark the RHI pipeline failed when popErrorScope reports an error. Also mark it failed when shader compilation reports an error. In prepareDraw, skip draws for failed pipelines and count them as skippedDraws with a one-time warning, so the failure stays per-draw as in master.

primary.reasoning:
I reproduced this at the RHI command level with two node tests. The last step, where the GPU throws away the frame, needs a real GPU. That step is defined behaviour in the WebGPU spec.

1) lumaDebugOff.test.ts builds a real luma `WebGPURenderPipeline` on a device object that uses the real `WebGPUDevice.prototype` with props.debug=false. This is how LumaRhiDevice.ts:113 creates the device. The native createRenderPipeline returns an invalid handle, and the native popErrorScope would report a GPUValidationError. The test shows:
- native pushErrorScope and popErrorScope are never called (luma no-ops them when debug is off, see node_modules/@luma.gl/webgpu/dist/adapter/adapter/webgpu-device.js:308-323);
- `linkStatus` becomes 'success' right away (webgpu-render-pipeline.js:41-51).
So `waitPipelineReady` (LumaRhiDevice.ts:1432-1450) resolves `ready` for a pipeline that failed validation or hit an internal error. The documented contract that `ready` rejects on failure is broken for this case.

2) failedPipelineDraw.test.ts runs the real `LumaRhiDevice` on a fake luma device whose shader reports a WGSL compile error. Output:
- `pipe.ready` rejects ("管线「lighting」:着色器「lighting」编译失败") and `isReady` is false;
- `runFrame` still records native.beginRenderPass, then native.setPipeline(<the failed pipeline>), native.draw(3), pass.end, encoder.finish and queue.submit;
- `runFrame` returns true, and stats show draws=1, skippedDraws=0.
`setPipeline` (LumaRhiDevice.ts:727-745) and `prepareDraw` (811-830) never check the pipeline's failure state or `isReady`. luma's `WebGPURenderPass.setPipeline` and `draw` (webgpu-render-pass.js:92-139) do not check either, and `draw` always returns true.

Under WebGPU rules this loses the whole frame. A shader module that failed to compile, or a pipeline that failed validation, is an invalid object. `setPipeline` with an invalid object invalidates the render pass. `pass.end()` on an invalid pass invalidates the parent GPUCommandEncoder. `finish()` then returns an invalid command buffer, and `queue.submit` rejects the whole submission. `runFrame` records every pass of a frame into a single command list (LumaRhiDevice.ts:1204-1253, `_submit` at 686-688). So every frame that draws with the failed pipeline shows a cleared or undefined canvas instead of losing only that one draw.

Master handles this differently. Pixi GL's generateProgram.mjs:30-32 only calls `logProgramError` when linking fails. A later `useProgram` or draw with that program raises a GL error for that call only, and the rest of the frame renders.

The branch's own intent matches master: src/engine2d/gpu/Pipelines.ts:114-116 says "失败的管线在录制时照常报错" (a failed pipeline reports an error when recorded). In practice nothing throws during recording. The draw goes through and poisons the command buffer.

Does the game hit this path: yes. Every engine2d draw goes through src/engine2d/gpu/WebGPURenderer.ts:269-284 (`pass.setPipeline(this.pipelines.get(cmd.pipeline))`, then `setBindings`, then `draw`/`drawIndexed`). No step checks pipeline status. The trigger is a shader or pipeline that fails on a particular GPU or driver: an FXC/DXC or Tint error, an internal error on a large lighting shader, or a stricter validation rule in a newer browser. The game's current shaders compile on the dev and test setups (parity suites pass), so this is a hardware-dependent robustness gap, not a failure every user sees. When it does trigger, the result is much worse than on master: a whole-screen blackout instead of one missing object or filter. Medium fits.

primary.fix_suggestion:
Minimal fix that keeps parity with master:
1. **Listen for loss.** In engine2d's createRenderer (src/engine2d/gpu/createRenderer.ts), subscribe to `rhi.lost`.
2. **Recreate the device on the same canvas.** Call `luma.createDevice` again with the same createCanvasContext options.
